commit message:
[catboost] Pool quantization on YT
- changes in quantized pool on disk format
- added column types
- added quantization schema (borders)
- other minor changes to allow effective digest calculation (to estimate memory usage for
training)
- support for Catboost DSV YT pool format

How to read this change list:
- `catboost/libs/quantized_pool/file_format.md` -- describes quantized pool format on disk
- `catboost/libs/quantized_pool` -- quantized pool [de]serialization and human readable format
- `catboost/yandex_specific/idl/pool` -- quantized pool format on YT
- `catboost/yandex_specific/libs/quantization` -- quantization on YT
- `proto` -- describes transposed pool format on YT
- `transpose_catboost_yt_dsv_op.cpp` -- map operation to transpose Catboost YT DSV pool
- `quantize_catboost_yt_dsv_pool.cpp` -- reduce operation to calculate quantization schema and
control flow for quantization on YT
- `apply_quantization_schema_op.cpp` -- map operation to apply quantization schema to transposed
pool
- `io.cpp` -- describes how to download quantized pool from YT to disk; also provides a function
calculate disk size upper bound for quantized pool.
- `catboost/yandex_specific/libs/quantization_main` -- defines cli interface for operations on
quantized pool
- `catboost/yandex_specific/tools/pool_ops` -- tool to work with quantized pools
- `catboost/yandex_specific/tools/pool_ops/test` -- tests for tool

`catboost/idl/pool/proto/column_types.proto` -- partially duplicates `EColumn` but provides
generated [de]serialization functions (otherwise I had to provide them by hand).

Since both quantization schema and columns info are protobuf they both can be viewed in YQL viewer
given quantized pool: https://yql.yandex-team.ru/Operations/WyDSCp3udoGocM6BuwJXxixkjAr2MJL4ESjMtSd4-9M=

author: Kostya Bazhanov <yazevnul@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
[catboost/java] Make error handing in shared library thread safe

There was a potential race condition in shared library. Exception message is stored in a singleton,
thus if error happens in two Java threads that use shared library simultaneously we had a data race
on TErrorMessageHolder::Message, there are a number of ways to solve this problem:
- introduce a mutex inside singleton, but I'm not sure if util locks, or any C++ locks in general
will cooperate with Java threads
- use thread local singletons, but again, I'm not sure if FastTlsSingleton will work with Java
threads
- make all CatBoostModel methods synchronized; I don't quite understand this part of Java, but it
sure look costly
- do the way it's done in this patch :)

Now all native functions return a String, if return value is null then everything is OK, if return
value is not null then something bad happened and return value contains an error message.

This will also allow end user to get error message exactly for his invocation of native method.

MLTOOLS-2242

commit message:
Do not set -fsanitize=fuzzer for FUZZ units. DEVTOOLS-4632

-fsanitize=fuzzer is equivalent to -fsanitize-coverage=x,y,z [1]. If used, it
should be used globally. Otherwise if ya make is invoked with
e.g. --sanitize-coverage=trace-pc-guard, non-FUZZ units will be instrumented
with different coverage functions than FUZZ units. libfuzzer7 can not work with
that.

To support testing the corpus without coverage, [2] is backported to libfuzzer-5.0.

[1] 5: https://a.yandex-team.ru/arc/trunk/arcadia/contrib/libs/clang5/lib/Driver/SanitizerArgs.cpp?rev=3826905#L288
6: https://a.yandex-team.ru/arc/trunk/arcadia/contrib/libs/clang6/lib/Driver/SanitizerArgs.cpp?rev=4014826#L323-324
7: https://a.yandex-team.ru/arc/trunk/arcadia/contrib/libs/clang7/lib/Driver/SanitizerArgs.cpp?blame=true&rev=4024667#L351-352

commit message:
[catboost] support training on quantized pool with large quantization grids

MLTOOLS-2656

Feature layout now contains some info on number of bins of quantized features, thus it's able to generate indices for artificial features generated from quantized features with more than 256 bins. When loading quantized pool loader will take quantized feature with more than 256 bins and generate artificial features from it (each artificial feature contains less than 256 bins) and then based on remapping from feature layout will pass them to dataset builder with appropriate arguments.

Lets assume that we have two features a and b, and feature a has more than 256 bins after quantization while feature b has less than 256. Now feature layout will be following:

a_0_255 b a_255_510 a_510_765 ...

e.g. for each feature with number of bins > 256 we add artificial features to the end of feature list.

commit message:
Add CYTHONIZE_PY directive to compile .py files with cython. DEVTOOLS-5157

This is needed by gevent which makes significant speedups by cythonizing py files:
https://github.com/gevent/gevent/commit/99541fd64e9cb0f0751cbe9a85f49eed1a2f1bd3

This is not equivalent to renaming .py to .pyx, as cython parses them in
different ways.

The files are added to pyxs (which is either pyxs_c or pyx_cpp) and not to
pyxs_c because althogh .py files can be compiled to C, the associated .pxd
files may require C++.

ref:3f360fa1213f6a628dce4d584ced94b26f9f1960

Move extra deps from library/python/runtime to contrib/libs/python. DEVTOOLS-5301

bytecode compiler.

contrib/libs/python has become the core of all arcadia python programs due to
all PEERDIR(contrib/libs/python) in ymake.core.conf. It should depend on
library/python/symbols/module and symbols/python. (They were incorrectly
specified as dependencies of library/python/runtime/main, even though they are
needed for python programs with custom main.) It has to be split in order to let
them use contrib/libs/python/Include.

author: orivej <orivej@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Harmonize importers, fix resfs_read in py2, resfs_resolve and get_data in py3

resfs_read should only accept resfs file paths.

resfs_resolve should also accept absolute paths.

get_data should not use resfs_read with Y_PYTHON_SOURCE_ROOT-relative (or
absolute) paths because they are not resfs paths, but it has to use resfs_read
without Y_PYTHON_SOURCE_ROOT. This works in both cases only if path ==
resfs_src(path, resfs_file=True). Since pkgutil.get_data requires
root-relative-based paths, if it works without Y_PYTHON_SOURCE_ROOT, then it
also works with it.

The implementation is now documented at
https://wiki.yandex-team.ru/devtools/commandsandvars/resourcefiles/

The issue was reported at
https://ml.yandex-team.ru/thread/devtools/169729410956600102/

commit message:
util/network/pollerimpl.h: add edge-triggered mode

In edge-tiggered mode poller notifies only about new events.

To restart notification call Set() with CONT_POLL_EDGE_TRIGGERED and
CONT_POLL_BACKLOG_EMPTY if previous read returned EAGAIN, truncated
result, or we read whole request and client shouldn't send more.
If backlog is empty then this is noop for backends "epoll" and "kqueue".
While backed "select" could emulate edge-triggered semantics.

Also add CONT_POLL_MODIFY to let "epoll" skip redundant EPOLL_CTL_ADD.

This PR updates the libgit2 version in contrib/libs using yamaker. The yamaker work is done by @kikht. Since pygit2 depends on libgit2 and there is version incompatibilities, this also updates pygit2 to a latest version.

We update libgit2 because we want to use some latest APIs in Arc.

The latest version of pygit2 tries to load ssl certificates and hence fails to build. So this also reverts changes done in https://github.com/libgit2/pygit2/pull/884/files. The commit hash which undoes those changes is `bfc74b6b05a308652f2b94b2b6ccfb5d3245ddfe`.

commit message:
Working contrib/* PEERDIR policies

* CHECK_DEPENDENT_DIRS macro was ignored for a long time and
constraints from the contrib/ya.make are not satisfied by the
current code.
* CHECK_DEPENDENT_DIRS implementation for DEVTOOLS-1200 is going
to forbid this macro usage out of module definition and it
must be removed from contrib/ya.make before merge to prevent
configure errors in all builds.

There are two choices:
1. Copy actualised contrib constraints into each contrib/**/ya.make
with module defininition (~~17k files)
2. Use nontransitive PEERDIR policy checks for contrib which should
depend only to libraries inside itsel with small number of exceptions

This commits follows secon approach.

author: Andrey Khalyavin <halyavin@gmail.com>
commit message:
Update libcxx to r366000

* Faster metaprogramming inside libc++.
*
* Fix SFINAE constraints for std::optional.
* Restrict string_view hashers only to standard character traits.
* Change return value of std::forward_list.remove(), std::list.remove() and alike methods from void to size_t.
* Implement a lot of bit operations.
* Fixes for tuple constructors when dealing with types which can be used in conversions but not constructors.
* constexpr swap
* make mutex and cond variables destructors trivial (on some platforms)
* deduction guides for unordered_set
* fix memory leak in set and map. It only happens when initializing from std::initializer_list which contains equivalent elements.

Workarounds:
* MSVC sometimes thinks that sizeof...(Arg) is a type pack instead of a number. So I hid sizeof using a wrapper.
* CUDA says that it is clang but doesn't support __is_same. So I switched it to non-clang path. Also CUDA libraries use libc++ internals. I added missing libc++ internals again with CUDA ifdefs.

author: Mikhail Borisov <borisov.mikhail@gmail.com>
commit message:
Cleanup `-fsigned-char` flag setting. Fixes default ARM7 builds with older GCC

* Remove `-fsigned-char` from ymake.core.conf (it is supposed to be compiler-agnostic)
* Make `-fsigned-char` independent of compiler version

By convention, whether `char` is signed depends on target OS and ARCH.
On most platforms it defaults to signed, except ARM and PPC (among
platforms supported by Arcadia).

Clang defines it in `isSignedCharDefault()` function:
https://github.com/llvm-mirror/clang/blob/5cee329c981f3e365e69fef3b05e43144df8a6e2/lib/Driver/ToolChains/Clang.cpp#L1254-L1283

GCC defines it as a static per-platform macro:
https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/blob/master/gcc/config/arm/arm.h#L1936

ref:094af9fd049264da07471753a7ca685b90541972

author: Mikhail Borisov <borisov.mikhail@gmail.com>
commit message:
Enable function-level section GC in `minsizerel` build mode

These flags lead to overall binary size decrease in large applications
with a lot of potentially dead code. Enabling these only in size-focused
`minsizerel` mode, as they trade compilation efficiency for reduced binary size.

* Generate per-function sections at compile time via
`-ffunction-sections -fdata-sections`. This is expected to increase
intermediate object file size and slow down compilation a bit.
* Enable link-time section GC via `-Wl,--gc-sections`. This is expected
to slow down linking a bit.

commit message:
using catboost for multi label classification

Tried using catboost in the Flu Shot Learning: Predict H1N1 and Seasonal Flu Vaccines competition hosted by drivendata.org.
The problem was a multi-label classsification , the goal is to predict the probablity of the individuals receiving their H1N1 and seasonal flu vaccines. The dataset included 35 features and the evaluation metric was roc_auc_score. The training and testing data alongwith the submission format file can be found on the website : https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/66/flu-shot-learning/page/211/

Since, the data had alot of categorical columns with upto 22 unique levels of categories, i wanted to try catboost and it worked wonders even with just the basic setting and ranked 29th. Later, with a advanced bagging approach, it ranked 24th with the submission score of 0.8620. The results were very exciting for me because no other boosting algorithm performed as good as catboost. Catboost not only gave the highest score but also had the least training and prediction time than the rest.

No other algorithm has worked so good with categorical data and it was very easy to implement also, there was no need to encode the categorical values and no need of alot of data preprocessing just eliminating nan values is enough.

I am very happy to use this library and thought i would share my experience. Hope turns out to be useful for others. This is the first time i'm contributing to an open source project, please bear with my mistakes and let me know of the changes. I'll be availabel at : ayachitsayee@gmail.com

commit message:
Add ASSERT macro and slighly improve USE_VANILLA_PROTOC handling

This needed to let vanilla protobuf disable `OPTIMIZE_PY_PROTO`.
In original version there was a value dependency loop `BUILD_PROTO_AS_EVLOG` drives `PROTO_CMD`, that depends in some cases on `OPTIMIZE_PY_PROTO` than becomes dependent on negative value of `BUILD_PROTO_AS_EVLOG` since `USE_VANILLA_PROTOC` was in `otherwise` part of the trigger.

Now `USE_VANILLA_PROTOC` and `BUILD_PROTO_AS_EVLOG` are separate triggers and so setting `OPTIMIZE_PY_PROTO` under `USE_VANILLA_PROTOC` now won't depend on `BUILD_PROTO_AS_EVLOG`.

author: spreis <spreis@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Fix induced deps for protobuf

`PROTO_SOURCE_INCLUDES`/`PROTO_HEADER_INCLUDES` are not resolved (always treated as path from arcadia root). For STL headers like `algorithm` this is obviously incorrect.
Since .proto files may be used in modules without all needed ADDINCLs we don't want to rely on resolving, so the simplest way is just to remove these from explicit lists. The dependencies on these headers won't be lost since these files are transitively includes by other files in the list and the latter will be parsed for dependencies appropriately.
- The `algorithm` is included by `google/protobuf/wire_format_lite_inl.h` in protobuf and `google/protobuf/extension_set.h` in protobuf_std
- `string` and `limits` are included by `google/protobuf/repeated_field.h` in protobuf_std.

Also induced deps for protobuf_std were written incorrectly: in absence of resolving relative paths just don't work

author: Mikhail Borisov <borisov.mikhail@gmail.com>
commit message:
Embed linker map into target binary

Pass along linker map contents as a binary's section, so it can later be used in packaging and CI. Handling "sidecar files" alongside binaries is not supported well by ya make. Instead, these files are embedded into the target binary as non-mapped PROGBITS sections.

Two flags are added:
* `EMBED_LINKER_CREF` (like former `DUMP_LINKER_CREF`): dump object-symbol cref graph into `.ya.linker_cref` section.
* `EMBED_LINKER_MAP` (like former `DUMP_LINKER_MAP`): dump linker map into `.ya.linker_map.` section (where LINKER_TYPE is `lld`, `gold` or `bfd`).

ref:61a97918728ed1dcf5dbb3c98fb9f7f9272a742a

author: dmtrmonakhov <dmtrmonakhov@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
vmexec: add kernel-release directory support

Arcadia now has directory infra/kernel/releases which contains resources of released kernels
Each release contains three entries
- vmlinuz
- initrd.img  : tiny initrd with minimal number of modules and overlay_root support
- modules.sqfs: squashfs with kernel modules

Now it is possible to boot existing rootfs, but with with custom kernel

Example:

$ ./infra/qemu/vmexec/vmexec -w / -K infra/kernel/releases/4.19/4.19.119-30  -- uname -a
Linux qavm-3b9e0eb7.qemu 4.19.119-30 #1 SMP Thu Apr 30 07:30:08 UTC 2020 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

$ ./infra/qemu/vmexec/vmexec -w / -K infra/kernel/releases/5.4/5.4.38-2  -- uname -a
Linux qavm-b96c3a20.qemu 5.4.38-2 #1 SMP Mon May 4 10:02:29 UTC 2020 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

kvm-init allow us to boot directrly from porto layrs which are packed as squashfs.

Example:
$ ./infra/qemu/vmexec/vmexec -w / -K ./infra/kernel/releases/5.4/5.4.38-2
-I ./infra/environments/rtc-bionic/release/vm-layer-nk/layer.squashfs
--trap

Welcome to Ubuntu 18.04.5 LTS (GNU/Linux 5.4.38-2 x86_64)
root@qavm-da8a7d39:~# mount | grep "root"
root on / type overlay (rw,relatime,lowerdir=/ovl_rootfs:/ovl_modules,upperdir=/media_rw/up,workdir=media_rw/work)

commit message:
Allow to run py.test with arcadia packages

PyCrypto package is used for tests here: https://github.yandex-team.ru/InfraComponents/mds-proxy-qa/blob/cb5baa11b059a1ba7bedac238d3db05a0b35b79f/tests/api/aes_256_cbc_decrypt.py#L3.
Without this mds proxy tests failed with:
"
from Crypto.Cipher import _AES
E   ImportError: cannot import name _AES
"

The reason is that _AES is a ".so" file, and pymds cannot imported this.
Probably there is a way to allow arcadia python interpretator to work with already installed ".so" files, but documentation doesn't help about this.

Also when PyCrypto was marked as deprecated here https://st.yandex-team.ru/SUBBOTNIK-2976,
author doesn't recommend a single replacement (neither I spent enough time to find one),
so one more exception for tests shouldn't be a problem.

normal cache poisoning to build commands. This enables build-time
guarantee that build artifact only contains "consistent" paths.

author: Mikhail Borisov <borisov.mikhail@gmail.com>
commit message:
Fix legacy (pre-macro-prefix-map) `__FILE__` macro substitution

`rootrel` was not working properly, because path was not marked as input
(in such cases, `rootrel` works as `basename`). Adding `input` attribute
breaks vcs_info, because vcs_info generation purposely bypasses build
graph via `_SRC_c_nodeps` compile command.

Move consistent-build macro subsitutions to compile command top level,
so they can be stripped from `_SRC_c_nodeps`.

ref:f6a9b51465f04a311f98f26cfa14cebb3d9fe31b

author: svidyuk <svidyuk@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
EXCEPT modificator for CHECK_DEPENDENT_DIRS

`EXCEPT` modificator allows to add prefix or Ant style glob exception for the `CHECK_DEPENDENT_DIRS` `DENY` restrictions

```
CHECK_DEPENDENT_DIRS(DENY PEERDIRS
bad/libs
EXCEPT bad/libs/some/good/libs/in/bad/place
)
```
will restrict everything in `bad/libs` except subdirectories of `bad/libs/some/good/libs/in/bad/place`

```
CHECK_DEPENDENT_DIRS(DENY PEERDIRS
bad/libs
EXCEPT GLOB **/good-*
)
```
will restrict everything in `bad/libs` except peers with last directory name starting from `good-` prefix (`PEERDIR(bad/libs/some/good-lib)` is allowed but `PEERDIR(bad/libs/some/good-framefork/lib)` is not)

author: thegeorg <thegeorg@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Generate object api for flatbuffers

This is for tensorflow compatibility, but may also be used for similar purposes in regular Arcadia code.
Excerpt from [flatbuffers manual](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/blob/master/docs/source/CppUsage.md#object-based-api--flatbuffers_cpp_object_based_api):

> FlatBuffers is all about memory efficiency, which is why its base API is written around using as little as possible of it. This does make the API clumsier (requiring pre-order construction of all data, and making mutation harder).
>
> For times when efficiency is less important a more convenient object based API can be used (through --gen-object-api) that is able to unpack & pack a FlatBuffer into objects and standard STL containers, allowing for convenient construction, access and mutation.

The flag turns on emission of `TensorT` class (in addition to regular `Tensor`) for `table Tensor`.

ref:2aa022b8bd497d86723753f6ccc46c286ec792bc

commit message:
[libc++] #include : omit inline namespace __y1 (fix for MSVC)

The MSVC compiler supposes that `partial_ordering` and other orderings lie inside the `std` namespace.
But in libc++ there is an intermediate namespace `__y1` marked as inline, thus now we have `std::__y1::partial_ordering` instead of just `std::partial_ordering`.
That's why three-way comparison (spaceship operator ``) produces a compilation error. See an example in the ticket.

commit message:
Support Huber loss computation on GPU

In this PR Huber loss is supported on GPU.

**Metrics** (time / loss value) for **three datasets** (allstate / msrank / year prediction) can be found here: https://proxy.sandbox.yandex-team.ru/2034219200.

In `cuda/tagers/ut/test_huber.cpp` there is a test which compares Huber loss score calculated on CPU to one which was calculated on GPU. Since test for the Huber loss is quite similar to the test for the Tweedie loss, general logic is separated in the `cuda/targets/ut/loss_functions_gpu_helper.h` file.

Two new tests for Python module were added in `python-package/ut/medium/test.py` and `pytest/cuda_tests/test_gpu.py`.

commit message:
Implementation of CUDA kernel for computing quantiles

**In this version an implementation of quantile computing on GPU in CUDA kernel is presented.**

An overall algorithm is the following: we take all objects targets and weights and bins at which objects are located. Then, in each bin, we sort the targets (and move the weights accordingly) in ascending order. Then, for each bin we calculate prefix sums of weights and finally launch a kernel which uses binary search for finding the lower bound and selecting the target.

Moreover, additional kernels are implemented for calculating weights with targets for MAPE loss, for calculating need weights with using `alpha` from loss description and for making a buffer with flags where positive number corresponds to the beginning of the offset.

Experiments were made on three datasets: MSRank, Year Prediction and AllState for both **doc parallel** and **feature parallel** cases. In this experiments we compare exact estimation on CPU with [previous CPU & GPU implementation from this PR](https://a.yandex-team.ru/arc/commit/7750254) and with current version with new kernels. Also the timing for computing the Gradient leaves estimation on the GPU is presented.

See experiments results: https://proxy.sandbox.yandex-team.ru/1995809163.

commit message:
Speed up copying derivatives for custom objectives

Performance was tested on the following example

mytest.pyx file: https://controlc.com/f0f5eb6e

import numpy as np
from mytest import *

N = 2000
pairs = [(float(i), float(i + 1)) for i in range(N)]
np_pairs = np.array(pairs)

In [1]: timeit sum_pairs_list(pairs)
10000 loops, best of 3: 66.8 µs per loop

In [2]: timeit sum_pairs_list(np_pairs)
1000 loops, best of 3: 1.58 ms per loop

In [3]: timeit sum_pairs_list_optimized(pairs)
100000 loops, best of 3: 14.1 µs per loop

In [4]: timeit sum_pairs_list_optimized(np_pairs)
100000 loops, best of 3: 9.91 µs per loop

#else

commit message:
Fix TFileInput::ReadTo() for pipes, sockets etc.

`TFile::Read()` tries to fill the supplied buffer completely by repeatedly calling `TFile::RawRead()`, which may cause a hang in `TFileInput::ReadTo()` if the underlying file is a pipe or socket.
This patch fixes the problem by avoiding `TFile::Read()`.

author: valbon <valbon@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
SK-5072: Build openssl for default-win-i686.

Asm files were generated with following configuration:
```
perl Configure no-makedepend no-tests -static VC-WIN32-masm
```

Where VC-WIN32-masm was created on the model of VC-WIN64A-masm and is following:
```
"VC-WIN32-masm" => {
inherit_from     => [ "VC-noCE-common", asm("x86_asm"),
sub { $disabled{shared} ? () : "uplink_common" } ],
AS               => "ml",
ASFLAGS          => "/nologo /Zi",
asoutflag        => "/Fo",
asflags          => "/Cp /coff /c /Cx",
sys_id           => "WIN32",
bn_ops           => add("BN_LLONG"),
perlasm_scheme   => "win32",
# "WOW" stands for "Windows on Windows", and "VC-WOW" engages
# some installation path heuristics in windows-makefile.tmpl...
build_scheme     => add("VC-WOW", { separator => undef }),
}
```

Some asm files, namely ecp_nistz256-x86.masm and poly1305-x86.masm, were generated with errors, so I had to remove -DECP_NISTZ256_ASM and -DPOLY1305_ASM.

author: Mikhail Borisov <borisov.mikhail@gmail.com>
commit message:
Link compiler-rt/builtins as a part of our `libcxxrt` runtime

This fixes pthread_exit() unwinding crashes on ARMv7 with glibcxx runtime
(similar to https://github.com/android/ndk/issues/1441 )

Both compiler-rt/builtins and libgcc implement builtins; since both of
them have `__gcc_personality_v0`, the one in libgcc must be used with
`glibcxx` C++ runtime.

author: Mikhail Borisov <borisov.mikhail@gmail.com>
commit message:
Enable DCE in linker by default

Enable link-time dead code elimination by default for all build modes.
* All functions and data are put in separate sections at compile time (`-ffunction-sections -fdata-sections`)
* Input sections unreachable by references are removed from the resulting binary by the linker. (`-Wl,--gc-sections`). This step can be disabled by `NO_LINKER_DCE` ymake flag.

Caveats:
* CGO linker fails with `--gc-sections`, this step is not enabled for Go programs
* iOS uses `-fembed-bitcode` which is incompatible with `-ffunction-sections` etc.

* rename bit functions
* multiline regex support
* instantiating additional iostream members for char type.

* fix bug in std::linear_congruential_engine

* constexpr set_union, set_difference, set_symmetric_difference, merge
* add slice_array operator= valarray overload.
* implement missing bits for codecvt and codecvt_byname
* eliminate `using namespace chrono` in \.

* use using_if_exists attribute to handle missing libc functionality
* avoid using non-standard printf format inside libc++

* * add ranges::data and ranges::empty

* * add ranges::size and concept sized_range
* * add contiguous_iterator concept
* avoid obsolete result_type and binary_function in valarray
* deprecate std::iterator and remove it as a base class
* hide std::not1 and std::not2
* add [[standalone_debug]] to preserve debug information which would otherwise be optimized out.
* fix UB in std::countr_zero(__uint128_t)
* remove deprecated std::raw_storage_iterator
* remove weak_equality and strong_equality in ## which were not standardized

commit message:
Add options to capture LLD `--print-gc-sections`/`--print-icf-sections`

These options make LLD generate reports with names of sections that are completely removed by the DCE pass or deduplicated by the ICF pass.
Such reports can be used as a "code smell" signal to detect dead code or unused dependencies.

* Add wrapper script options to redirect the linker's stdout into a file
* Untie ICF from `minsizerel` build, enable it by `LINKER_ICF=yes` OR minsizerel mode
- Disabled by default; opt-in (opposite to DCE which is enabled by default and disabled by `NO_LINKER_DCE=yes`)
- No way to turn this off in minsizerel build with an option (no change here)
* Enable DCE report by `LINKER_DCE_PRINT_SECTIONS`
* Enable ICF report by `LINKER_ICF_PRINT_SECTIONS`
* Save linker's stdout to `.linker.txt` when either of the options above is enabled

author: Mikhail Borisov <borisov.mikhail@gmail.com>
commit message:
CPPCOM-48: Collect time trace json from compiler/linker commands

Introduce `ya make` vars:
* `TIME_TRACE`: Enable all known time tracing
* `COMPILER_TIME_TRACE`: Enable compiler time tracing (clang)
* `LINKER_TIME_TRACE`: Enable linker time tracing (lld)
* `TIME_TRACE_GRANULARITY`: Lower bound for event durations to be logged (microseconds; default: 500us)

When enabled, time trace reports are collected into `.time_trace.json` files for each traced command and can be extracted for analysis with `--add-result .time_trace.json`.

Initial version of DYNAMIC_LIBRARY support

This  multimodule creates dynamically linkable library for arcadia build including

author: thegeorg <thegeorg@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Remove -fcommon and explicitly enable the default -fno-common behavior

The use of a "common" section to match up tentative object definitions in different translation units in a program is contrary to the C standards (section 6.9p5 in C99 and C11, section 6.7 in C90), gives a high risk of error, may lead to poorer quality code, and provides no benefits except backwards compatibility with ancient code.

Unix C compilers have traditionally allowed "int x;" in file a.c to be allocated by the linker to the same storage as "int x;" in file b.c when these two C files are linked together.  gcc supports this if "-fcommon" is enabled, which is the default on most targets.  But it is contrary to the C (and C++) standards that say there shall be exactly /one/ definition of each object.  And it is very easy to have errors in code by accidentally having duplicate names in different files (if the programmer has not used "static"), perhaps even of different types.  With "-fno-common", such errors are caught at link time.

Also, data in common sections will hinder some types of optimisation, such as "-fsection-anchors".

Surely [it is time](https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=85678#c0) to make "-fno-common" the default, at least when a modern C standard is specified indicating that the code is modern?  People who need the old behaviour can always get it with "-fcommon".

commit message:
Introduce TThread::CurrentThreadNumericId()

`CurrentThreadId()` returns unique identifier via `pthread_self()`. On Linux it is equal to `std::this_thread::id()`.

Various Linux utilities (e. g. `top` and `ps`) use different (numeric) thread identifiers coming from `gettid()` or `syscall(SYS_gettid())`.
This PR introduces a method for getting such numbers.

commit message:
Update libc++ to 352c3af3 (8 Oct 2021).

Notable changes:
* remove non-conforming atomic_fetch_add and atomic_fetch_sub extensions
* use std::addressof instead of & to protect against operator overloading
* add bool, char, integer and string formatters
* use init_priority(100) when possible for initialization
* add string_view constructor from any contiguous range
* refactor exception throwing in std::string and std::vector
* don't autodetect pthreads on MinGW, allow user to configure it instead with LIBCXX_HAS_PTHREAD_API=ON
* enable operator in ranges::transform and ranges::iota
* implement unicode support in formatting functions
* remove LIBCPP_CONSTEXPR markings on starts_with() etc. since it is C++17 functionality
* add std::views::common range adaptor
* properly implement comparison functions like is_eq
* simplify std::ranges::subrange
* use enable_if_t instead of enable_if in span
* simplify comparison enums in compare header

* throw correct exception from std::vector::reserve

commit message:
[util] fix fstat for archive directories on windows

Currently TFileStat has a bunch of problems on Windows:
1. Mode computation ORs different types, but file attributes it checks are not mutually exclusive. E.g. it is possible for directory to have both `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY` and `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE`, but it will currently lead to invalid `_S_IFDIR | _S_IFREG` mode.
2. Any file with `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT` flag is considered to be symlink. But there are many other types of reparse points even user-defined ones. For more info see https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/reparse-point-tags

To fix all this we do the following:
1. Add `ReparseTag` field to `TSystemFStat` and fill it for reparse points in `GetStatByHandle`.
2. Refactor `GetWinFileType` out of `GetFileMode` to ensure that we always select only single `S_IFMT` value.
3. Pass reparse tag value into `GetWinFileType` and select `S_IFLNK` only for `IO_REPARSE_TAG_SYMLINK` and `IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT` tags. The latter one is a bit strange, but this behaviour is aligned with current implementation of `WinReadLink`.
4. Factor `ReadReparsePoint` out of `WinReadLink`. This function uses `DeviceIoControl` to read reparse point data into structures copied from WDK.
5. Add `WinReadReparseTag` that uses `ReadReparsePoint` to extract reparse point tag. We use this approach instead of MSDN-recommended `FindFirstFile` because latter requires file path, but we have file handle at this point. AFAIK golang and python use similar approach for this.
6. Add test for archived directory case.
7. Make symlink nofollow tests run only when symlink creation is possible for current user.

Discovered in https://st.yandex-team.ru/ARC-3931

commit message:
Update libc++ to 529a7930 (10 Dec 2021).

Notable changes:
* use "= delete" for functions marked as "// = delete"
* remove _LIBCPP_DEFAULT, we can just use "= default"
* make views::counted SFINAE-friendly
* remove unneeded std:: from
* fix the return value of max_size()
* workaround for clang in transform_view
* implement special.mem.concepts
* add range constructor for string_view
* make __wrap_iter constexpr
* make sequence contrainers for SFINAE-friendly
* reduce binary size in  header
* fix uniform_int_distribution for 128-bit result type
* remove support for clang 9 and older
* add missing `__format__` attributes
* implement three-way comparison for std::reverse_iterator
* avoid overload resolution in path comparison operators
* fix constraints for string_view iterator/sentinel constructor
* value initialize unique_ptr deleter_type

Update libc++ to 1fe897df (21 Dec 2021).

* allow __move_constexpr to work with unrelated pointers
* add deprecation warnings to ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT and ATOMIC_VAR_INIT

* disable _LIBCPP_DEBUG_ASSERT during constant evaluation
* add GCC workaround for std::char_traits::length() which doesn't support constexpr builtin
* enable optimized _IsSame on GCC and Clang
* implement monadic operations for std::optional
* use _LIBCPP_DEBUG_ASSERT in string header instead of _LIBCPP_ASSERT
* implement ranges::uninitialized_default_construct{,_n}
* add inline to basic_string::shrink_to_fit
* make __swap_allocator constexpr
* make __compressed_pair fully constexpr
* remove goto from std::string
* make ThrowingIterator constexpr
* fix noexcept in __decay_copy
* improve workaround for init_priority((100)) outside of system headers

commit message:
DEVTOOLSSUPPORT-18626: In venv directly call Py_BytesMain()

The arcadia main function (library/python/runtime_py3/main/main.c::pymain) calls Py_InitializeFromConfig() before going to the vanilla python Py_Main().
Py_InitializeFromConfig() overrides sys.prefix and sys.exec_prefix by default values ('/var/empty') and then import __res module (and importer.pxi as a part of it).
importer.pxi::_init_venv() set a proper value to sys.prefix and sys.exec_prefix attributes.
Py_Main() in turn also calls Py_InitializeFromConfig() and reset the sys attributes to their default values again.
I don't know why it was not a problem in python 3.9 but in 3.10 it is.

author: spreis <spreis@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Try to remove SET_COMPILE_OUTPUTS_MODIFIERS macro

The macro was used to change modifiers on compile outputs (namely object files).
The only use of macro was to add `norel` modifier, which changes the way how output paths are constructed.
- W/o the modifier (default case) output path is always localized to module and disambiguated by use of `__` for `..` and `_` for `.` in path to file relative to module (the latter rule is only applied when file is in subdirectory to disambiguate outputs from same input in nested modules).
- W/ modifier output path is exact match to input path (only changing `$S` to `$B` if input is from source tree).

Generally norel is dangerous but needed in 2 major cases
- The output is produced by tool which lacks ability to control output path and always deduce output path from input (protoc being prominent example)
- The input is not directly in module and output is used in source code (not consumed by build system) e.g. header file generation from input in subdirectory.

The macro was introduced along with strict disambiguation for outputs to cure problematic cases. However it is now used only in one case and seemingly to just contract path on Windows (disambiguation resulted in lengthy path due to distant relative references in aforementioned module).  Build system now supports long paths on Windows, so this case shouldn't be a problem any more.

ref:d9bd16f903a360389ec2a0ad207eae4a5abae442

author: Andrey Khalyavin <halyavin@gmail.com>
commit message:
Update libc++ to 34313583 (20 Feb 2022).

Notable changes:
* replace _LIBCPP_INLINE_VISIBILITY with _LIBCPP_HIDE_FROM_ABI in __filesystem/operations.h
* implement sortable and mergeable concepts
* replace __uncvref with __uncvref_t
* implement consistent stateful allocator behavior in std::basic_string::operator+
* remove some _LIBCPP_CXX03_LANG ifdef's
* move _LIBCPP_ASSERT related code to a separate file
* enable std::hash in C++11 mode
* make algorithm includes more granular
* implement range functionality for std::istream_iterator
* add debug check in basic_string::insert
* replace "" with  in includes in src/ files for consistency with include/
* add push/pop macros defines in src/ files for consistency with include/
* add availability annotations to optional operations
* remove conditional noexcept from view_interface --- this is allowed by the standard
* replace _LIBCPP_SAFE_STATIC with _LIBCPP_CONSTINIT
* guard most of std::ranges under _LIBCPP_HAS_NO_INCOMPLETE_RANGES
* remove priority pragma for AIX from locale.cpp because it is ignored anyway

author: spreis <spreis@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
[YMAKE-214] Enable strict output includes resolution

This enables strict resolving of output includes ymake feature.
- Output includes will be resolved only as includes (not as inputs) and when applied (not when parsed).
- from_input modifier tells ymake to resolve output_includes as inputs and early. This is needed for macros where output includes are also inputs

This is needed to mitigate cases like TAXICOREINFRA-2129: early resolving of output_includes may match to lower-priority but readily available header instead of higher priority one which is not available in graph at the time of this early resolving (it will be available at the time of late resolving).

The fixes applied:
- JOIN_SRCS , GENERATE_ENUM_SERIALIZATION and GENERATED_SRCS naturally require output includes from inputs because they actually include their inputs into outputs
-  XS_PROTO  need proper steering of its induced deps to match its ADDINCL, so they explicitly made C++
- ORM code generation also includes inputs into output, but was done using generic PYTHON macro. To avoid generic macro parameters extension I've just added special macro with the same meaning, removed boilerplare and duplicate scripts,  moved script to scripts/ and made it python3.
- contrib/python/autobahn, mds/mastermind/... and code in dummy_arcadia generated incudes  that not actually match output_includes specified.

author: spreis <spreis@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Add ASSERT macro and slighly improve USE_VANILLA_PROTOC handling

This needed to let vanilla protobuf disable `OPTIMIZE_PY_PROTO`.
In original version there was a value dependency loop `BUILD_PROTO_AS_EVLOG` drives `PROTO_CMD`, that depends in some cases on `OPTIMIZE_PY_PROTO` than becomes dependent on negative value of `BUILD_PROTO_AS_EVLOG` since `USE_VANILLA_PROTOC` was in `otherwise` part of the trigger.

Now `USE_VANILLA_PROTOC` and `BUILD_PROTO_AS_EVLOG` are separate triggers and so setting `OPTIMIZE_PY_PROTO` under `USE_VANILLA_PROTOC` now won't depend on `BUILD_PROTO_AS_EVLOG`.

ref:c1fbd2b1c5b8992f6c29ff87640f5ae38c137406

author: spreis <spreis@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Fix induced deps for protobuf

`PROTO_SOURCE_INCLUDES`/`PROTO_HEADER_INCLUDES` are not resolved (always treated as path from arcadia root). For STL headers like `algorithm` this is obviously incorrect.
Since .proto files may be used in modules without all needed ADDINCLs we don't want to rely on resolving, so the simplest way is just to remove these from explicit lists. The dependencies on these headers won't be lost since these files are transitively includes by other files in the list and the latter will be parsed for dependencies appropriately.
- The `algorithm` is included by `google/protobuf/wire_format_lite_inl.h` in protobuf and `google/protobuf/extension_set.h` in protobuf_std
- `string` and `limits` are included by `google/protobuf/repeated_field.h` in protobuf_std.

Also induced deps for protobuf_std were written incorrectly: in absence of resolving relative paths just don't work

author: Mikhail Borisov <borisov.mikhail@gmail.com>
commit message:
Embed linker map into target binary

Pass along linker map contents as a binary's section, so it can later be used in packaging and CI. Handling "sidecar files" alongside binaries is not supported well by ya make. Instead, these files are embedded into the target binary as non-mapped PROGBITS sections.

Two flags are added:
* `EMBED_LINKER_CREF` (like former `DUMP_LINKER_CREF`): dump object-symbol cref graph into `.ya.linker_cref` section.
* `EMBED_LINKER_MAP` (like former `DUMP_LINKER_MAP`): dump linker map into `.ya.linker_map.` section (where LINKER_TYPE is `lld`, `gold` or `bfd`).

author: dmtrmonakhov <dmtrmonakhov@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
vmexec: add kernel-release directory support

Arcadia now has directory infra/kernel/releases which contains resources of released kernels
Each release contains three entries
- vmlinuz
- initrd.img  : tiny initrd with minimal number of modules and overlay_root support
- modules.sqfs: squashfs with kernel modules

Now it is possible to boot existing rootfs, but with with custom kernel

Example:

$ ./infra/qemu/vmexec/vmexec -w / -K infra/kernel/releases/4.19/4.19.119-30  -- uname -a
Linux qavm-3b9e0eb7.qemu 4.19.119-30 #1 SMP Thu Apr 30 07:30:08 UTC 2020 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

$ ./infra/qemu/vmexec/vmexec -w / -K infra/kernel/releases/5.4/5.4.38-2  -- uname -a
Linux qavm-b96c3a20.qemu 5.4.38-2 #1 SMP Mon May 4 10:02:29 UTC 2020 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

kvm-init allow us to boot directrly from porto layrs which are packed as squashfs.

Example:
$ ./infra/qemu/vmexec/vmexec -w / -K ./infra/kernel/releases/5.4/5.4.38-2
-I ./infra/environments/rtc-bionic/release/vm-layer-nk/layer.squashfs
--trap

Welcome to Ubuntu 18.04.5 LTS (GNU/Linux 5.4.38-2 x86_64)
root@qavm-da8a7d39:~# mount | grep "root"
root on / type overlay (rw,relatime,lowerdir=/ovl_rootfs:/ovl_modules,upperdir=/media_rw/up,workdir=media_rw/work)

commit message:
Allow to run py.test with arcadia packages

PyCrypto package is used for tests here: https://github.yandex-team.ru/InfraComponents/mds-proxy-qa/blob/cb5baa11b059a1ba7bedac238d3db05a0b35b79f/tests/api/aes_256_cbc_decrypt.py#L3.
Without this mds proxy tests failed with:
"
from Crypto.Cipher import _AES
E   ImportError: cannot import name _AES
"

The reason is that _AES is a ".so" file, and pymds cannot imported this.
Probably there is a way to allow arcadia python interpretator to work with already installed ".so" files, but documentation doesn't help about this.

Also when PyCrypto was marked as deprecated here https://st.yandex-team.ru/SUBBOTNIK-2976,
author doesn't recommend a single replacement (neither I spent enough time to find one),
so one more exception for tests shouldn't be a problem.

author: svidyuk <svidyuk@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
EXCEPT modificator for CHECK_DEPENDENT_DIRS

`EXCEPT` modificator allows to add prefix or Ant style glob exception for the `CHECK_DEPENDENT_DIRS` `DENY` restrictions

```
CHECK_DEPENDENT_DIRS(DENY PEERDIRS
bad/libs
EXCEPT bad/libs/some/good/libs/in/bad/place
)
```
will restrict everything in `bad/libs` except subdirectories of `bad/libs/some/good/libs/in/bad/place`

```
CHECK_DEPENDENT_DIRS(DENY PEERDIRS
bad/libs
EXCEPT GLOB **/good-*
)
```
will restrict everything in `bad/libs` except peers with last directory name starting from `good-` prefix (`PEERDIR(bad/libs/some/good-lib)` is allowed but `PEERDIR(bad/libs/some/good-framefork/lib)` is not)

DEVTOOLS-7586

author: thegeorg <thegeorg@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Generate object api for flatbuffers

This is for tensorflow compatibility, but may also be used for similar purposes in regular Arcadia code.
Excerpt from [flatbuffers manual](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/blob/master/docs/source/CppUsage.md#object-based-api--flatbuffers_cpp_object_based_api):

> FlatBuffers is all about memory efficiency, which is why its base API is written around using as little as possible of it. This does make the API clumsier (requiring pre-order construction of all data, and making mutation harder).
>
> For times when efficiency is less important a more convenient object based API can be used (through --gen-object-api) that is able to unpack & pack a FlatBuffer into objects and standard STL containers, allowing for convenient construction, access and mutation.

The flag turns on emission of `TensorT` class (in addition to regular `Tensor`) for `table Tensor`.

commit message:
[libc++] #include : omit inline namespace __y1 (fix for MSVC)

The MSVC compiler supposes that `partial_ordering` and other orderings lie inside the `std` namespace.
But in libc++ there is an intermediate namespace `__y1` marked as inline, thus now we have `std::__y1::partial_ordering` instead of just `std::partial_ordering`.
That's why three-way comparison (spaceship operator ``) produces a compilation error. See an example in the ticket.

author: ri-ri <ri-ri@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Implementation of CUDA kernel for computing quantiles

**In this version an implementation of quantile computing on GPU in CUDA kernel is presented.**

An overall algorithm is the following: we take all objects targets and weights and bins at which objects are located. Then, in each bin, we sort the targets (and move the weights accordingly) in ascending order. Then, for each bin we calculate prefix sums of weights and finally launch a kernel which uses binary search for finding the lower bound and selecting the target.

Moreover, additional kernels are implemented for calculating weights with targets for MAPE loss, for calculating need weights with using `alpha` from loss description and for making a buffer with flags where positive number corresponds to the beginning of the offset.

Experiments were made on three datasets: MSRank, Year Prediction and AllState for both **doc parallel** and **feature parallel** cases. In this experiments we compare exact estimation on CPU with [previous CPU & GPU implementation from this PR](https://a.yandex-team.ru/arc/commit/7750254) and with current version with new kernels. Also the timing for computing the Gradient leaves estimation on the GPU is presented.

See experiments results: https://proxy.sandbox.yandex-team.ru/1995809163.

Speed up copying derivatives for custom objectives

import numpy as np
from mytest import *

N = 2000
pairs = [(float(i), float(i + 1)) for i in range(N)]
np_pairs = np.array(pairs)

10000 loops, best of 3: 66.8 µs per loop

In [2]: timeit sum_pairs_list(np_pairs)
1000 loops, best of 3: 1.58 ms per loop

In [3]: timeit sum_pairs_list_optimized(pairs)
100000 loops, best of 3: 14.1 µs per loop

In [4]: timeit sum_pairs_list_optimized(np_pairs)
100000 loops, best of 3: 9.91 µs per loop

author: valbon <valbon@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
SK-5072: Build openssl for default-win-i686.

Asm files were generated with following configuration:
```
perl Configure no-makedepend no-tests -static VC-WIN32-masm
```

Where VC-WIN32-masm was created on the model of VC-WIN64A-masm and is following:
```
"VC-WIN32-masm" => {
inherit_from     => [ "VC-noCE-common", asm("x86_asm"),
sub { $disabled{shared} ? () : "uplink_common" } ],
AS               => "ml",
ASFLAGS          => "/nologo /Zi",
asoutflag        => "/Fo",
asflags          => "/Cp /coff /c /Cx",
sys_id           => "WIN32",
bn_ops           => add("BN_LLONG"),
perlasm_scheme   => "win32",
# "WOW" stands for "Windows on Windows", and "VC-WOW" engages
# some installation path heuristics in windows-makefile.tmpl...
build_scheme     => add("VC-WOW", { separator => undef }),
}
```

Some asm files, namely ecp_nistz256-x86.masm and poly1305-x86.masm, were generated with errors, so I had to remove -DECP_NISTZ256_ASM and -DPOLY1305_ASM.

Link compiler-rt/builtins as a part of our `libcxxrt` runtime

This fixes pthread_exit() unwinding crashes on ARMv7 with glibcxx runtime
(similar to https://github.com/android/ndk/issues/1441 )

Both compiler-rt/builtins and libgcc implement builtins; since both of
them have `__gcc_personality_v0`, the one in libgcc must be used with
`glibcxx` C++ runtime.

author: Mikhail Borisov <borisov.mikhail@gmail.com>
commit message:
Enable DCE in linker by default

Enable link-time dead code elimination by default for all build modes.
* All functions and data are put in separate sections at compile time (`-ffunction-sections -fdata-sections`)
* Input sections unreachable by references are removed from the resulting binary by the linker. (`-Wl,--gc-sections`). This step can be disabled by `NO_LINKER_DCE` ymake flag.

Caveats:
* CGO linker fails with `--gc-sections`, this step is not enabled for Go programs
* iOS uses `-fembed-bitcode` which is incompatible with `-ffunction-sections` etc.

commit message:
Add options to capture LLD `--print-gc-sections`/`--print-icf-sections`

These options make LLD generate reports with names of sections that are completely removed by the DCE pass or deduplicated by the ICF pass.
Such reports can be used as a "code smell" signal to detect dead code or unused dependencies.

* Add wrapper script options to redirect the linker's stdout into a file
* Untie ICF from `minsizerel` build, enable it by `LINKER_ICF=yes` OR minsizerel mode
- Disabled by default; opt-in (opposite to DCE which is enabled by default and disabled by `NO_LINKER_DCE=yes`)
- No way to turn this off in minsizerel build with an option (no change here)
* Enable DCE report by `LINKER_DCE_PRINT_SECTIONS`
* Enable ICF report by `LINKER_ICF_PRINT_SECTIONS`
* Save linker's stdout to `.linker.txt` when either of the options above is enabled

commit message:
CPPCOM-48: Collect time trace json from compiler/linker commands

Introduce `ya make` vars:
* `TIME_TRACE`: Enable all known time tracing
* `COMPILER_TIME_TRACE`: Enable compiler time tracing (clang)
* `LINKER_TIME_TRACE`: Enable linker time tracing (lld)
* `TIME_TRACE_GRANULARITY`: Lower bound for event durations to be logged (microseconds; default: 500us)

When enabled, time trace reports are collected into `.time_trace.json` files for each traced command and can be extracted for analysis with `--add-result .time_trace.json`.

commit message:
Initial version of DYNAMIC_LIBRARY support

This  multimodule creates dynamically linkable library for arcadia build including
- PEERDIR behavior as for LIBRARY.
- Build of dynamic library
- Transfer of all dynamic libraries to final targets (PROGRAMS and other dynamic libraries). This e.g. enables seamless testing of PROGRAMS of such libraries.
- This is now opt-in using `WITH_DYNAMIC_LIBS() ` macro due to performance considerations. Also default when OPENSOURCE is set.
- This doesn't currently work transitively through DYNAMIC_LIBRARY. If DYNAMIC_LIBRARY has transitive dependencies to another DYNAMIC_LIBRARY it should use new DYNAMIC_DEPS macro to enable propagation of such libraries to PROGRAMs as results. This is because final targets like DLL stop propagation of PEERDIRs and other properties (w/o this PEERDIRs of DLLs would leak to PROGRAMS). We will try to invent properties that propagate through such modules and collect .so names as such properties.
- Properties of such library are transferred by dependencies including licence-related properties, ADDINCL(GLOBAL ) etc.

author: thegeorg <thegeorg@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Remove -fcommon and explicitly enable the default -fno-common behavior

The use of a "common" section to match up tentative object definitions in different translation units in a program is contrary to the C standards (section 6.9p5 in C99 and C11, section 6.7 in C90), gives a high risk of error, may lead to poorer quality code, and provides no benefits except backwards compatibility with ancient code.

Unix C compilers have traditionally allowed "int x;" in file a.c to be allocated by the linker to the same storage as "int x;" in file b.c when these two C files are linked together.  gcc supports this if "-fcommon" is enabled, which is the default on most targets.  But it is contrary to the C (and C++) standards that say there shall be exactly /one/ definition of each object.  And it is very easy to have errors in code by accidentally having duplicate names in different files (if the programmer has not used "static"), perhaps even of different types.  With "-fno-common", such errors are caught at link time.

Also, data in common sections will hinder some types of optimisation, such as "-fsection-anchors".

Surely [it is time](https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=85678#c0) to make "-fno-common" the default, at least when a modern C standard is specified indicating that the code is modern?  People who need the old behaviour can always get it with "-fcommon".

ref:e25d21a1e92bfaebd17bde1240c721c92495fda7

commit message:
Update libc++ to 1e628d0c (25 Sep 2021).

Update default allocator for THashMap since volatile allocators are not allowed. The problem is triggered by THashMap with TAtomic values which is a volatile type.

Notable changes:
* do not enable P1951 until C++23 since it is a breaking change
* remove _LIBCPP_HAS_NO_VARIABLE_TEMPLATES, assume they are always available
* implement std::pair::operator
* fix __wrap_iter to be a proper contiguous iterator
* remove _LIBCPP_INLINE_VAR, assume inline variables are always available
* disallow volatile types in std::allocator
* add some missing _LIBCPP_HIDE_FROM_ABI
* remove locale fallbacks for AIX
* do not make counting_semaphore default constructible
* add parser std-format-spec
* avoid ub-inducing asserts in constexpr in char_traits::copy
* eliminate _LIBCPP_EQUAL_DELETE, assume =delete always available
* add missing wchar functions for z/OS

commit message:
Introduce TThread::CurrentThreadNumericId()

`CurrentThreadId()` returns unique identifier via `pthread_self()`. On Linux it is equal to `std::this_thread::id()`.

Various Linux utilities (e. g. `top` and `ps`) use different (numeric) thread identifiers coming from `gettid()` or `syscall(SYS_gettid())`.
This PR introduces a method for getting such numbers.

author: Andrey Khalyavin <halyavin@gmail.com>
commit message:
Update libc++ to 352c3af3 (8 Oct 2021).

Notable changes:
* remove non-conforming atomic_fetch_add and atomic_fetch_sub extensions
* use std::addressof instead of & to protect against operator overloading
* add bool, char, integer and string formatters
* use init_priority(100) when possible for initialization
* add string_view constructor from any contiguous range
* refactor exception throwing in std::string and std::vector
* don't autodetect pthreads on MinGW, allow user to configure it instead with LIBCXX_HAS_PTHREAD_API=ON
* enable operator in ranges::transform and ranges::iota
* implement unicode support in formatting functions
* remove LIBCPP_CONSTEXPR markings on starts_with() etc. since it is C++17 functionality
* add std::views::common range adaptor
* properly implement comparison functions like is_eq
* simplify std::ranges::subrange
* use enable_if_t instead of enable_if in span
* simplify comparison enums in compare header

commit message:
Update libc++ to dce5fc56 (11 Nov 2021).

Notable changes:
* remove non-standard methods _FilesystemClock::to_time_t/from_time_t and add file_clock::to_sys/from_sys instead
* remove gc support
* use addressof instead of &
* implement printing volatile pointers
* fix segmentation fault in __do_put_integral
* inline most of `__vector_base` into `vector`
* fix hang in counting_semaphore::try_acquire
* tidy up money_get::__do_get's sign parsing
* refactor num_put::do_put to reduce duplication
* add preferred_name attribute to basic_format_context
* add check for view_interface template parameter to be a valid view
* tweak template argument deduction for span constructors
* fix behavior of tanh(complex) and exp(complex) on infinity

commit message:
[util] fix fstat for archive directories on windows

Currently TFileStat has a bunch of problems on Windows:
1. Mode computation ORs different types, but file attributes it checks are not mutually exclusive. E.g. it is possible for directory to have both `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY` and `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE`, but it will currently lead to invalid `_S_IFDIR | _S_IFREG` mode.
2. Any file with `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT` flag is considered to be symlink. But there are many other types of reparse points even user-defined ones. For more info see https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/reparse-point-tags

To fix all this we do the following:
1. Add `ReparseTag` field to `TSystemFStat` and fill it for reparse points in `GetStatByHandle`.
2. Refactor `GetWinFileType` out of `GetFileMode` to ensure that we always select only single `S_IFMT` value.
3. Pass reparse tag value into `GetWinFileType` and select `S_IFLNK` only for `IO_REPARSE_TAG_SYMLINK` and `IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT` tags. The latter one is a bit strange, but this behaviour is aligned with current implementation of `WinReadLink`.
4. Factor `ReadReparsePoint` out of `WinReadLink`. This function uses `DeviceIoControl` to read reparse point data into structures copied from WDK.
5. Add `WinReadReparseTag` that uses `ReadReparsePoint` to extract reparse point tag. We use this approach instead of MSDN-recommended `FindFirstFile` because latter requires file path, but we have file handle at this point. AFAIK golang and python use similar approach for this.
6. Add test for archived directory case.
7. Make symlink nofollow tests run only when symlink creation is possible for current user.

Discovered in https://st.yandex-team.ru/ARC-3931

commit message:
Update libc++ to 529a7930 (10 Dec 2021).

Notable changes:
* use "= delete" for functions marked as "// = delete"
* remove _LIBCPP_DEFAULT, we can just use "= default"
* make views::counted SFINAE-friendly
* remove unneeded std:: from
* fix the return value of max_size()
* workaround for clang in transform_view
* implement special.mem.concepts
* add range constructor for string_view
* make __wrap_iter constexpr
* make sequence contrainers for SFINAE-friendly
* reduce binary size in  header
* fix uniform_int_distribution for 128-bit result type
* remove support for clang 9 and older
* add missing `__format__` attributes
* implement three-way comparison for std::reverse_iterator
* avoid overload resolution in path comparison operators
* fix constraints for string_view iterator/sentinel constructor
* value initialize unique_ptr deleter_type

* add inline to basic_string::shrink_to_fit
* make __swap_allocator constexpr
* make __compressed_pair fully constexpr
* remove goto from std::string
* make ThrowingIterator constexpr
* fix noexcept in __decay_copy
* improve workaround for init_priority((100)) outside of system headers

commit message:
DEVTOOLSSUPPORT-18626: In venv directly call Py_BytesMain()

The arcadia main function (library/python/runtime_py3/main/main.c::pymain) calls Py_InitializeFromConfig() before going to the vanilla python Py_Main().
Py_InitializeFromConfig() overrides sys.prefix and sys.exec_prefix by default values ('/var/empty') and then import __res module (and importer.pxi as a part of it).
importer.pxi::_init_venv() set a proper value to sys.prefix and sys.exec_prefix attributes.
Py_Main() in turn also calls Py_InitializeFromConfig() and reset the sys attributes to their default values again.
I don't know why it was not a problem in python 3.9 but in 3.10 it is.

author: spreis <spreis@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
Try to remove SET_COMPILE_OUTPUTS_MODIFIERS macro

The macro was used to change modifiers on compile outputs (namely object files).
The only use of macro was to add `norel` modifier, which changes the way how output paths are constructed.
- W/o the modifier (default case) output path is always localized to module and disambiguated by use of `__` for `..` and `_` for `.` in path to file relative to module (the latter rule is only applied when file is in subdirectory to disambiguate outputs from same input in nested modules).
- W/ modifier output path is exact match to input path (only changing `$S` to `$B` if input is from source tree).

Generally norel is dangerous but needed in 2 major cases
- The output is produced by tool which lacks ability to control output path and always deduce output path from input (protoc being prominent example)
- The input is not directly in module and output is used in source code (not consumed by build system) e.g. header file generation from input in subdirectory.

The macro was introduced along with strict disambiguation for outputs to cure problematic cases. However it is now used only in one case and seemingly to just contract path on Windows (disambiguation resulted in lengthy path due to distant relative references in aforementioned module).  Build system now supports long paths on Windows, so this case shouldn't be a problem any more.

ref:d9bd16f903a360389ec2a0ad207eae4a5abae442

commit message:
Update libc++ to eaadc451 (4 Feb 2022).

Notable changes:
* fix chrono::duration constructor constraint
* delete base class for std::basic_string
* add ranges::in_out_out_result and ranges::in_in_out_result
* implement indirectly_copyable{,_storable} concepts
* rename __referenceable to __can_reference to match text of the standard
* add _LIBCPP_HAS_NO_CONCEPTS guards where concepts are used
* simplify no concepts guards
* add specifications for basic_common_reference and common_type for pair
* make _VSTD an alias for std so that it can be removed in the future
* remove std from friend declaration to facilitate switch from _VSTD to std
* fix TOCTOU issue with std::filesystem::remove_all
* add additional constraints to std::ranges::get for subranges when N == 0
* pick unique bit for __regex_word constant
* use vsnprintf instead of _vsnprintf on Windows
* ADL-proof ranges::iter_swap and ranges::iter_move
* implement std::ranges::distance
* merge _LIBCPP_HAS_NO_RANGES into _LIBCPP_HAS_NO_CONCEPTS

author: Andrey Khalyavin <halyavin@gmail.com>
commit message:
Update libc++ to 34313583 (20 Feb 2022).

Notable changes:
* replace _LIBCPP_INLINE_VISIBILITY with _LIBCPP_HIDE_FROM_ABI in __filesystem/operations.h
* implement sortable and mergeable concepts
* replace __uncvref with __uncvref_t
* implement consistent stateful allocator behavior in std::basic_string::operator+
* remove some _LIBCPP_CXX03_LANG ifdef's
* move _LIBCPP_ASSERT related code to a separate file
* enable std::hash in C++11 mode
* make algorithm includes more granular
* implement range functionality for std::istream_iterator
* add debug check in basic_string::insert
* replace "" with  in includes in src/ files for consistency with include/
* add push/pop macros defines in src/ files for consistency with include/
* add availability annotations to optional operations
* remove conditional noexcept from view_interface --- this is allowed by the standard
* replace _LIBCPP_SAFE_STATIC with _LIBCPP_CONSTINIT
* guard most of std::ranges under _LIBCPP_HAS_NO_INCOMPLETE_RANGES
* remove priority pragma for AIX from locale.cpp because it is ignored anyway

author: spreis <spreis@yandex-team.ru>
commit message:
[YMAKE-214] Enable strict output includes resolution

This enables strict resolving of output includes ymake feature.
- Output includes will be resolved only as includes (not as inputs) and when applied (not when parsed).
- from_input modifier tells ymake to resolve output_includes as inputs and early. This is needed for macros where output includes are also inputs

This is needed to mitigate cases like TAXICOREINFRA-2129: early resolving of output_includes may match to lower-priority but readily available header instead of higher priority one which is not available in graph at the time of this early resolving (it will be available at the time of late resolving).

The fixes applied:
- JOIN_SRCS , GENERATE_ENUM_SERIALIZATION and GENERATED_SRCS naturally require output includes from inputs because they actually include their inputs into outputs
-  XS_PROTO  need proper steering of its induced deps to match its ADDINCL, so they explicitly made C++
- ORM code generation also includes inputs into output, but was done using generic PYTHON macro. To avoid generic macro parameters extension I've just added special macro with the same meaning, removed boilerplare and duplicate scripts,  moved script to scripts/ and made it python3.
- contrib/python/autobahn, mds/mastermind/... and code in dummy_arcadia generated incudes  that not actually match output_includes specified.

ref:41af7aad2e93e2011ba1d1a9c6c1fdb4b28ddc1e

commit message:
add ability to use test filter list from file

для opensource YDB очень важно иметь возможность не запускать некоторые тесты. Сейчас это можно сделать через аргументы командой строки, но это для нас не удобно по причине того, что нам необходимо будет для включения/исключения теста запускать cmake, и конфиг для исключения тестов с CMake получается очень раздутый и не удобный.

я предлагаю добавить опцию и переменную окружения, в котором будет передаваться имя файла со списком enabled/disabled тестов.

author: dskor <dskor@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
Reuse SSL

Сохраняем SSL сессию рядом с сокетом, в котором она заведена.
В кэше вращаем не сокеты, а TConnection ( socket, ssl, hostAddr ).

Сервис RMS (применяет риск-правила в частности для выдачи сплита на маркете) использует глубоко внутри себе Neh для выполнения запросов.
Сервис Saturn (хранит в себе скоры пользователей и умеет применять простенькие модельки), в который ходит RMS, предоставляет **только https** интерфейс (т.к. передаются перс данные и иногда кросс-дц).

Сейчас наблюдаем дополнительные ~12ms на p99 связанные с постоянными установками соединений. Хочется спилить эти 12ms до того, как начнутся распродажи (черная пятница/кибер понедельник) и нагрузка вырастит кратно ( маркет говорит про x8 ).

author: dskor <dskor@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
Add carry to catboost

=== Carry:
Преобразуем **одномерные oblivious tree** подставляя значения **float фичей не участвующих в Ctr** с целью **зафиксировать сетку значений факторов**.

Вход: (одномерная модель неважного в какой loss обученная) и (сетка факторов {feature_name:[values]})
Выход: модель размерности числа точек в фиксируемой сетке факторов
Disclamer: **сейчас ломаем weights**

- CLI: https://a.yandex-team.ru/arcadia/mlp/overdraft/utils/carry
- Код: https://a.yandex-team.ru/arcadia/mlp/overdraft/utils/catboost_modifications/carry.cpp
- Кубик: https://nirvana.yandex-team.ru/alias/yoverdraft-make-carry-model (с исправлением cd)
- Inner кубик: https://nirvana.yandex-team.ru/operation/2b595c91-9a40-47df-b1e7-7a471b18b857

=== Uplift:
Преобразуем **одномерные oblivious tree** подставляя значения **float фичей не участвующих в Ctr** с целью **посчитать разность сырых скоров между фиксируемыми точками**.

Вход: (одномерная модель неважного в какой loss обученная) и (две точки в подпространстве факторов [feature_name], [base_value], [next_value])
Выход: одномерная модель
Disclamer: **сейчас ломаем weights**

- CLI: https://a.yandex-team.ru/arcadia/mlp/overdraft/utils/uplift
- Код: https://a.yandex-team.ru/arcadia/mlp/overdraft/utils/catboost_modifications/uplift.cpp
- Кубик: https://nirvana.yandex-team.ru/operation/e3ed17b0-6fc4-436a-8327-49f82f4d10d4 (с исправлением cd)

Check SSL close and wait for bidirection shutdown to prevent RST

Возвращаем сохранение сессий #3
Коллеги из RMS столкнулись с аномальным ростом отказов внешних сервисов, а именно ФинЦЕРТ и mfm и это послужило причиной отката предыдущей версии из : https://a.yandex-team.ru/review/4446891/details

В рамках этого PR:
1) добавляем проверку валидности https. соединения, на случай, если сервер инициировал закрытие сессии (фактически в таком случае происходила ошибка записи очередного запроса, т.к. TLS соединение было уже закрыто). Такую ошибку можно воспроизвести локально, если поднять nginx с конфигом закрывающим соединение после выполнения запроса (эту ошибку починили).
2) Не создаем спекулятивно соединения, т.к. это приводит к долгому ожиданию Client Hello на стороне сервера и последующему отстрелу RST клиенту (при отправке Client Hello). Для пользователя выглядит как ошибка в handshake

author: thegeorg <thegeorg@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
Provide proper jni.h by the means of library/cpp/jni

As jni.h provides extreme ABI compatibility, there is no need to use jdk to build JNI modules.

This PR replaces complex logic of finding necessary jni with the following code (already present in [library/cpp/jni/ya.make](https://arcanum.yandex-team.ru/arcadia/library/cpp/jni/ya.make).

```
IF (OS_ANDROID)
    # Do nothing, use jni.h shipped with NDK
ELSE()
    PEERDIR(
        contrib/libs/jdk
    )
ENDIF()
```

Remaining dependencies on contrib/libs/jdk will be removed in further PRs and using of JDK interface will be restricted in favor of this library.

NB: PEERDIRing `library/cpp/jni` will also provide a couple of utility sources which are not used by catboost at the time.

commit message:
[catboost]: Get rid of implicitly declared default copy constructor in order to avoid -Wdeprecated-copy error

https://timsong-cpp.github.io/cppwp/n4659/depr.impldec

```
The implicit definition of a copy constructor as defaulted is deprecated if the class has
a user-declared copy assignment operator or a user-declared destructor. The implicit definition
of a copy assignment operator as defaulted is deprecated if the class has a
user-declared copy constructor or a user-declared destructor (15.4, 15.8).
In a future revision of this International Standard, these implicit definitions could become deleted (11.4).
```

It blocks update of standard library: https://a.yandex-team.ru/review/5084628/details

```
$(SOURCE_ROOT)/catboost/cuda/cuda_lib/cuda_base.h:291:9: error: definition of implicit copy assignment operator for 'TCudaDeviceProperties' is deprecated because it has a user-declared copy constructor [-Werror,-Wdeprecated-copy]
        TCudaDeviceProperties(const TCudaDeviceProperties& other) = default;
        ^
```

commit message:
Use `CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` flag to prune architectures

* Добавляю переменную `CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`, в которых указываю, для каких архитектур оставлять device-код в гпушных либах CUDA / cuDNN
* Выставляю для неё разумные дефолты для тех архитектур, которые потенциально страдают от избыточного размера кода (сейчас это 11.4, потом можно будет расширить для других архитектур)
* Пробрасываю эту переменную и путь до бинарника `nvprune` в скрипт линковки
* Ищу и пруню гпушные либы

Как проверить, что работает:
* например, успешно собирается `ya make --build=release -DTENSORFLOW_WITH_CUDA -DCUDA_VERSION=11.4 -DCUDNN_VERSION=8.0.5 -DCUDA_ARCHITECTURES=sm_70 yweb/webdaemons/ocrdaemon` (с дефолтным `-DCUDA_ARCHITECTURES` падает по relocation overflow)
* елси хочется посмотреть на изменение размеров, то можно собрать `ya make ml/zeliboba/libs/ynmt_lm/score/bin/ --build=relwithdebinfo -DCUDA_VERSION=11.4 -DCUDNN_VERSION=8.0.5` один раз с дефолтным значением, другой раз с `-DCUDA_ARCHITECTURES=sm_70,sm_80,compute_80` - размер бинаря уменьшится

Особенности:
* ~~Сейчас дефолт для каждой новой версии куды содержит в себе тупо все поддерживаемые архитектуры. Имеет смысл его порезать до чего-то более разумного~~ - порезал
* Обход аргументов в обратном порядке сделан для того, чтобы эмулировать поведение линкера (для линкера важен порядок пробрасывания между либами для линковки и директориями, в которых их нужно искать)
* ~~Сейчас артефакты прунинга кладутся рядом с оригинальными либами; возможно, стоит их складывать в отдельное место в build-директории, но я пока не разобрался как это делать; буду рад, если кто-то подскажет~~ уже неактуально - кладу в build_root
* nvprune имеет свойство мусорить варнингом в stderr, когда прунит `libcudart_static.a` (это норма - там нет кода, который можно было бы попрунить); как вариант можно закостылить и не прунить `libcudart_static.a`, но я открыт к предложениям

author: kickbutt <kickbutt@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
Bump CUDA -> 11.4 and cuDNN -> 8.0.5

~~большой~~ PR по переключению дефолтной версии CUDA с cuDNN в Аркадии

Обновляем CUDA: 10.1 -> 11.4
Обновляем cuDNN: 7.6.5 -> 8.0.5

Помимо простого обновления версий, данный PR содержит следующее:

* От перехода на CUDA 11.4 честно сломался только [один проект](https://a.yandex-team.ru/arcadia/cv/imgclassifiers/danet/backend/gpu_cuda?rev=rXXXXXX), поэтому просто там правим
* Где-то поменялись тесты на объём потребляемой памяти, поэтому их просто переканонизируем
* По поводу удаления таргетов из clang_prev_targets:
  - `ld.lld` из поставки clang14 не справляется с линковкой - не может найти символы в попруненных либах, хотя они там есть
  - но можно просто переключиться на автосборку, потому что те проблемы [совместимости cuDNN и clang](https://st.yandex-team.ru/#655b977f30316b33e3a5ec87), для которых gpu-шные таргеты добавляли в clang_prev_targets, в автосборке уже не существуют
* По поводу удаления таргетов из cuda11_targets - теперь cuda11_targets отличается от автосборки версией TensorRT (5 в автосборке vs 7 в cuda11) и режимом сборки (relwithdebinfo в автосборке vs release в cuda11), но есть два момента
  - те, таргеты, которые я удаляю, не зависят от TensorRT, поэтому их не имеет смысла их тестить и в автосборке, и в cuda11 (про таргет `ads/quality/sis/tests/cuda11_arch80` мне сейчас ничего не известно; если что - выпилим его отдельным таргетом)
  - на самом деле дублирование даже вредно - в `dict/mt/daemon/tests/gpu` есть тест на потребление памяти gpu, который имеет разные результаты в зависимости от release vs relwithdebinfo, поэтому для этого таргета мы в принципе не можем собираться одновременно и в автосборке, и в cuda11

По поводу дефолтной автосборки в принципе пришлось сделать четыре приседания:
* пишем кастомный скрипт для линкера:
  - идея скрипта: переставляем большую секцию с gpu-шным кодом (`.nv_fatbin`) после `.bss` (самая дальняя секция, куда можно ожидать ссылки из кода бинаря), чтобы было меньше шансов нарваться на проблемы с relocation overflow в (`.bss`)
  - замечание: в самом скрипте используем в нём только `INSERT AFTER`, чтобы [ld.ldd и дальше применял свои дефолтные правила для остальной программы](https://releases.llvm.org/16.0.0/tools/lld/docs/ELF/linker_script.html#sections-command)
  - сделал замеры перфа генезисного инференса через `ml/zeliboba/libs/ynmt_lm/translate/bin` на том сценарии, который оказался под рукой  - не заметил каких-то изменений
* добавляем nvcc-флаг `-Xfatbin=-compress-all`, чтобы наш fatbin сжимался и занимал меньше пространства в бинаре (далее он будет разжиматься на старте программы,  так что оверхеда быть не должно)
  - сделал замеры перфа генезисного инференса через `ml/zeliboba/libs/ynmt_lm/translate/bin` на том сценарии, который оказался под рукой  - не заметил каких-то изменений
* добавляем флаг линкера `--no-relax`, так как опция "relaxation of relocatable symbols" (когда мы load в регистр + jump по адресу в регистре заменяем на относительный jump) уменьшает допустимый диапазон оффсетов, которые мы можем кодировать, что также приводит к relocation overflow
  - больше информации можно найти в https://maskray.me/blog/2023-05-14-relocation-overflow-and-code-models
  - сделал замеры перфа генезисного инференса через `ml/zeliboba/libs/ynmt_lm/translate/bin` на том сценарии, который оказался под рукой  - не заметил каких-то изменений
* ещё чуть более гранулярно выпиливаем лобзиком архитектуры из либ в поставках CUDA / cuDNN - в категории "ассемблерный код" (`compute_XX`) оставляем только для последней версии поддерживаемой архитектуры (то есть `compute_86`), так как на новых GPU-шках мы будем JIT-компилироваться из него, а на старых GPU-шках мы возьмём готовый машинный код для них

Эти идеи были в основном взяты из следующих источников:
- https://maskray.me/blog/2021-07-04-sections-and-overwrite-sections#insert-before-and-insert-after и https://discourse.llvm.org/t/lld-relocation-overflows-and-nv-fatbin/58889 (про перемещение `.nv_fatbin`)
- https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-binary-utilities/index.html#nvprune (про `nvprune`)
- https://maskray.me/blog/2023-05-14-relocation-overflow-and-code-models#relocation-overflow (`-Wl,--no-relax`)
- https://discourse.llvm.org/t/lld-relocation-overflows-and-nv-fatbin/58889/6 + https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/43074/files#diff-1e7de1ae2d059d21e1dd75d5812d5a34b0222cef273b7c3a2af62eb747f9d20aR360 (про `-Xfatbin=-compress-all`)

Дополнительные комментарии:
- можно дополнительно не выпиливать ненужные архитектуры, но этот флаг дополнительно уменьшает размеры бинарей (например, таргет `ml/zeliboba/libs/ynmt_lm/translate/bin`уменьшается на 120 MiB, что составляет примерно 5% от размера бинаря)
- кастомный скрипт для линкера позволяет не развлекаться с ещё более гранулярным выпиливанием архитектур (например, для таргетов `TENSORFLOW_WITH_CUDA`)

Оставшийся технический долг, который будет делать в других PRах
* донести функциональность из `link_exe.py` в `link_dyn_lib.py`
* перейти на TensorRT 7
* выпилить cuda11_targets
* выпилить флаг `TENSORFLOW_WITH_CUDA` в пользу `CUDA_REQUIRED` и удалить tensorflow_with_cuda_targets (??)
* поднять версию стандарта c++ для гпушного кода с 14 до 17

author: spreis <spreis@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
Revertcommits

Эта история про второй питон подразнесла нам графогенерацию . Нам придется этот коммит откатить.

Суть проблемы в том, что генерация для 2го и 3го раньше была одной и той же командой. Ты сделал так, что команда стала разной, но аутпут этих двух команд одинаковый. Имя результата команды является ключом и сейчас берётся какая-то рандомная команда из двух. При этом команда влияет на UID и все UIDы питонячей протогенерации мигают. От фатальных проблем нас спасает только то, что protobuf-ы на самом деле одинаковые. И даже это не факт - сейчас ты патчишь какие-то рандомные либы включая таковые для 3го питона.

Мы тут конечно редиски - мы в целом контролируем клэши аутпутов, но не в мультимодулях - там часто бывает что одна и та же команда оказывается в нескольких вариантах мультимодуля (потому что оно по дефолту сейчас так себя ведёт). Мы хотим это зачинить (сделать отдельный подмодуль под кодген и отселить всякие RUN_PROGRAM туда) - но это много работы и мы не успели.

План такой:
1. мы откатываем твой фикс
2. отдельно стабилизируем раздельные команды генерации для 2го и 3го питона
3. накатываем обратно отревеченные тут правки.
916a5456c4e901ab2cda0841b4167e16397e83c4
