author: arkady-e1ppa <arkady-e1ppa@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
YT-21868: Refactor NYT::Format

NYT::Format had several problems:
1. There are too many ways to enable printing of T. Not all are equally good. You could specialize TValueFormatter, you could write an overload of FormatValue, you could write an overload of ToString, you could write an overload of operator << for special stream or you could specialize the Out function.
2. If you attempt to print T which cannot be printed, you get a linker error without a proper source location which is very frustrating to work with.
3. There is no static analysis of format string performed even when it is possible.
4. If you write FormatValue overload, you still have to write ToString overload if you want to use this function (and people tend to use it quite a bit, since it is defined for util types and enums.

This pr addresses these issues to some extent. Relevant changes:
1. The only way to support NYT::Format is to define the FormatValue overload. Otherwise, you get a compile-time error.
2. Format overloads have changed: Now you have two options for general use:
```
TString Format(TStaticFormat<TArgs...> fmt, TArgs&&... args);
TString Format(TRuntimeFormat fmt, TArgs&&... args);
```
Either overload checks if TArg has a FormatValue overload. TStaticFormat performs a compile-time check of flags and the argument count. It binds to any string literal and constexpr string/string_view (and TStringBuf). TRuntimeFormat has to be mentioned explicitly. Otherwise, you will get a compile-time error for using runtime variable as a format.

3(!!!). Types which name begins with NYT:: have a specialization of ToString function which uses FormatValue. Thus, if you write class in namespace NYT and define FormatValue, you get ToString automatically. If your type is not from namespace enclosing NYT, you can just call NYT::ToString for the same effect. This limitation was caused by the fact, that we cannot review all of the external projects code which might inherit from stl  classes or adopt some other questionable code practises which may completely break the dispatching mechanism of ToString due to the specialization (there were such cases). Proper documentation of this library will be added soon, so that this interaction is made known. This limitation might be lifted later
77beb68082e10aaf48be1842aad8aba63f26c1bd

author: spreis <spreis@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
Use same wine peerdir on Windows target regardless of host - take 2

This PR contains following changes:
1. Unconditional PEERDIR to wine for Windows-targeted builds. This is proven to align UIDs in cross and native builds on Windows for the vast majority of build nodes (.asm built by ml tool and its dependants are  the only notable exceptions as of now)
2. Wine is made host platform resource bundle. This more precisely reflects the nature of tools and allows per-host resource selection without effect on UIDs.
3. Wine  description is modernized to by-platform json and shared between ya,conf.json and ya.make
4. Separate archive added fpr Windows host to avoid unpacking issues of original archive caused by symlinks in it. This is needed because due totest now getting all transitive resources of their build and try to deliver these resources even though they are unused.  In initial experiments this caused tests failures on native Windows in attempts to unpack wine.
5. Brief description of wine resource peculiarities is added.
6. Wine tool reference is fixed in build commands. The resource ID was hardcoded in wine command prefix which is plainly incorrect.

Upon fixingwindows resources may be excluded from JSONs leaving only one platform.

Note to future readers: TError is not "perfect-forwarding" unfriendly class. This means that the code

template <class... TArgs>
TError MakeError(TArgs&&... args) {
  return TError(std::forward<TArgs>(args)...);
}
```
will not compile and needs to be properly adjusted (see. TError::Wrap for implementation example)

commit message:
ai_optimized.py

This commit introduces significant enhancements and updates to the `MultinomialFromUniform` and `ChoiceFromUniform` operations within the Theano-based sampling script. The main updates include the following:

1. Code Clean-Up and Optimization:
   - Unused Variables Removed: Local variables that were previously defined but never used in computations (`pvals`, `unis`, `n`) have been replaced with underscores (`_`) to comply with code standards and improve readability.
   - Unused Variable Handling: Unused variable `t` has been removed from the `c_code` method to clean up the code.

2. Error Handling and Validation Improvements:
   - Input Dimension Checks: Added checks to ensure that input dimensions of `pvals` and `unis` are valid, enhancing robustness and providing clearer error messages if the input does not meet the expected shape.
   - Validation for Sample Size: Added validation in `ChoiceFromUniform` to prevent sampling more items than available without replacement, ensuring the integrity of the sampling process.

3. AI-Driven Optimization:
   - Performance Enhancements: Optimized the `perform` method for both `MultinomialFromUniform` and `ChoiceFromUniform` to leverage AI-driven insights for efficient computation and better performance. This includes optimizing the cumulative sum calculations and sampling operations.

4. Choice Sampling Enhancements:
   - Replacement Option: Added the `replace` parameter to `ChoiceFromUniform` to allow sampling with or without replacement. This provides flexibility depending on the sampling needs.

5. Documentation and Examples:
   - Updated Documentation: Improved documentation within the code to better describe the purpose and usage of the updated operations.
   - Example Usage: Added example code at the end of the script to demonstrate the usage of the updated `MultinomialFromUniform` and `ChoiceFromUniform` operations with sample probability distributions and uniform samples.

Errors Found and Resolved:
- Unused Variables: The script contained several unused local variables which have been replaced with underscores to follow best practices.
- Unnecessary Assignment: The assignment to variable `t` was removed from the C code section since it was not used, cleaning up the code.

commit message:
AI_Build.py

Here in this fork, the script has been enhanced with many new features that are powered by Artificial Intelligence that help in enhancing the build process in different platforms. One of the key improvements is computerizing some of the decriminalization algorithms by the application of artificial intelligence. They help in smarter decision making regarding errors that occur during the build process and configurations changes that needs to be made thus minimal interference from a human being and enhance the efficiency of the build tool. This advancement helps in making the script more flexible to several build environments as well as to get over to several hard knitted situations with ease. 
 
 Another big change is the improvement of the cloud cross-platform compatibility. The script has been made even simpler to support more platforms that have caused headache on how to manage dependencies and configurations of different platforms. Some of these enhancements make it possible to run the build tool uninterrupted in notably different operating systems and settings. This means that while using the script, the error detection as well as the error resolution procedures vary depending on the platform in which the applications are made hence improving the prowess of the script. 
 
 Some issues which negatively impacted this scripts performance have been noted and fixed in this release. These fixes are associated with the environment detection problem, dependencies management and with error reporting. Therefore, the stability of the script has been enhanced with the view to having a more reliable and less variant script in the construction of building. They improves meretriciousness to reduce Level gg breaks for users and increase reliability during builds. 
 
 Further, the main script of this program has also been redesigned so that it becomes easy to read as well as maintain and at the same time fast. All the duplicated code has been eliminated, and major parts of the code respective to performance have been made lean. Technological change in this refactoring entails modification of the script and its underlying log system that enhances tracking and debugging. The completion of this kind of work brings about new changes that enhance script readability and flexibility by leaving spaces for modifications. 
 
 Also, the documentation has been revised to include the changes that have been incorporated in this version. Users are now able to receive clear instructions and examples regarding the changes made so they would know how to use them. This update to the documentation guarantees that users can easily adapt the enhanced script in their build processes and harness new enhancements made on it. 
 
 More specifically, these updates enable a more resilient, flexible, and smart build tool suitable for numerous applications. The improvements relate to the design and construction of the product, and make the build process less cumbersome for the end user, no matter which device they are using.

commit message:
YT-23346: Introduce YT_ASSUME and YT_UNREACHABLE macros.

Y_ASSUME and Y_UNREACHABLE macros are platform-independent ways to
give a hint for a compiler about some value or state. Compilier may
use that hint for optimization. On the other hand if the hint is
wrong it may lead to undefined behavior.

YT_ASSUME and YT_UNREACHABLE are wrappers around Y_ASSUME and
Y_UNREACHABLE that actually check that the hint is correct in
debug build. That introduces some code safety and at the same time
allows certain optimization in optimized build.

commit message:
Upgrade mimalloc to 1.8.7

Ниже описал существенные изменения в поведении, которые я заметил (в сравнении с версией 1.7.2, которая лежит в контрибах сейчас)

Полный changelog можно посмотреть в [readme.md](http://readme.md)

* Поменялся дефолт у [опции](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc/blob/9cae0d31cd28476664dbaa6e4e6940b9d900842a/src/options.c#L109), определяющей то, как неиспользуемая память возвращается в систему. В старых версиях по умолчанию использовался madvise с флагом MADV_FREE, в свежих версиях же используется MADV_DONTNEED. Это может вызвать неожиданные изменения (в худшую сторону) на графиках потребляемой анонимной памяти (), хотя по факту потребление должно быть \+- одинаковым

* Алгоритм работы аллокатора претерпел некоторые изменения. Например, мы споткнулись об то, что в новой версии mimalloc выделяет себе 1Gb (размер задается [опцией](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc/blob/2765ec93026f445cad8f38e6b196dd226a1f6e61/src/options.c#L87)) памяти при первой же аллокации. Само по себе это мало на что влияет, но неприятности могут случиться, если звать в начале программы mlockall

commit message:
Make sure returned TStringBuffers do not change during splitter lifetime. Also make input string reference const

<https://github.com/ydb-platform/ydb/issues/12306>

Make input string reference const

Make sure returned TStringBuffers do not change during splitter lifetime

splitter.Consume() возвращает TStringBuf.

Если в колонке есть ескейпинг кавычек, вся колонка обрамлена двойными кавычками (`"`), а внутри для ескейпинга двойных кавычек используются две идущие подряд двойные кавычки (`""`).

В таком случае вернуть TStringBuf, ссылающийся на кусок входящего TString, не получится, т.к. нужной подстроки в нем не существует.

Для этого используется мембер TVector\<TStringbuf\> CustomStrings. В него накидываются нужные кусочки из исходной строки и в конце складываются в мембер-строку TString CustomString

Например, из строки  `"abc""cde""efg"`  копились кусочки `abc"`, `cde"`, `efg` и в конце склеивались.

И возвращался TStringBuf из этой строки-мембера.

Проблема в том, что если в другой колонке той же строки также встречались кавычки с ескейпингом, эта строка-мембер CustomString очищалась. При том, что на неё всё еще ссылался возвращённый ранее TStringBuf.

В итоге "предыдущий" TStringBuf либо начинал ссылаться на часть новой строки, если новая строка была длиннее, либо на часть новой строки \+ рандомный набор байт в памяти, если новая строка оказывалась короче.

Фикс в том, чтобы хранить все строки, сгенерённые сплиттером, всё время жизни сплиттера
commit_hash:aa4957e1d8030cd48d06eaa16a7ad61e878348f8

author: arkady-e1ppa <arkady-e1ppa@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
YT-21233: Adjust (To/From)ErrorAttributeValue CPOs, revert ConvertTo becoming CPO, move TErrorCode and TError to library/cpp/yt/error

\[nodiff:caesar\]

List of changes:

 1) Make `ConvertTo` a normal function again (basically, a revert of previous change). It turned out to be very inconvenient entry point

 2) Introduce concept for "Primitive types" which are handled without yt/core module. Please note that inclusion of core **does not** affect work with primitive types (otherwise we would be facing and ODR violation). These are numerics, duration, instant, string-like objects and guid

 3) Introduce `FromErrorAttributeValue` which is a substitute to `ConvertTo` with special behavior (see below)

 4) Scheme for (de-)serialization has changed:

    1) Primitive types are handled via `ConvertToTextYsonString` and `ConvertFromTextYsonString`

    2) Other types are not supported without yt/core. Otherwise `ConvertToYsonString(value, EYsonFormat::Text)` used for serialization and `ConvertTo<T>(value)` for deserialization.

 5) New format of attribute value storage allows to not care about concrete type of the attribute (text yson strings can be detected since they start with `\"` and deserialized so are text yson bools, everything else is already human readable). This drops dependency on `TTokenizer`

 6) Some small parts (e.g. enums or constants or aliases) of yt/core/misc files were moved to library/cpp/yt/\* locations and re-included to drop dependencies of stripped\_error on them

 7) `TErrorAttributes` is now a simple hash map instead of a handle to `IAttributeDictionary`

 8) `ExtractFromAttributes` weak symbol is finally moved to library/cpp/yt/error due to point 9 allowing to fully drop dependency on `IAttributeDictionary`. Combined with point 7 this drops dep on yt/core/ytree altogether

 9) Moved `TErrorCode` to library/cpp/yt/error. There is a logger there which forces dep on library/cpp/yt/logging. It is not required really, and can be later removed

10) Moved `TError` with format and macroes to library/cpp/yt/error. It still (and probably forever will) depend on yson.

What can be done next: Switch TYsonString to TString and move ConvertTo/FromTextYsonString to library/cpp/yt/error. This would remove dep on library/cpp/yt/yson\_string
commit_hash:6f11dc478ab782a1f98a5aedcd45a4800d3f4e7b

author: tazjin <tazjin@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
allow local increases of libc++ hardening level

Restores the behaviour of setting `_DEFAULT` in our site config (as is [recommended](https://libcxx.llvm.org/Hardening.html#notes-for-vendors) for "vendors"), allowing users to increase the libc++ hardening level of their builds using certain flags.

This behaviour is required for our continuous migration towards higher hardening levels, as one-off hardening runs are otherwise significantly more difficult.

This commit does not change the behaviour of where hardening is enabled, meaning that it should have no effect on build targets in general (though some targets that are broken in trunk after enabling hardening may not be marked as such yet).

Refer to the ticket for further information.

author: swarmer <swarmer@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
check lifetimes of TStringBuf constructed from TString without taking into account copy-on-write semantics

`TString` is a copy-on-write type, which means that in some cases the valid lifetime of its data might extend beyond the lifetime of an individual `TString` (if it was copied).

However, there are practically no cases where this behaviour is appropriate, and leaving around an "owning" `TString` is undesirable.

Due to this behaviour we have previously refrained from enabling `[[clang::lifetimebound]]` for `TStringBuf` constructors, because some cases of view construction from a temporary `TString` were in fact valid.

This commit enables the check, as all existing related bugs in Arcadia have been fixed. Please see the related ticket and the announcement on Этушка (link will be in the post-commit comments) for more information.

Продолжение починки крэшей при форке

Ситуация такая же - используем subprocess для обработки данных ( subprocess не наши, написаны множеством команд на нескольких языках под конкретные ситуации), быстро избавиться от форка не получится. Есть шанс избавиться от этого пул треда, но тоже не быстро.

Тесты на это очень сложно написать, без больших изменений в тред пуле, пробовал с перехватом `pthread_atfork`, к сожалении, не только `TAtforkQueueRestarter` им пользуется и нормально перехватить тоже не получилось.

author: kulikov <kulikov@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
Try to workaround incorrect behavior for urls with @

By now, for urls like <http://localhost:80/search@zzz>, we treat everything after scheme and before '@' as userinfo, and zzz as host (because '/' is not considered as a right delimiter for userinfo). This doesn't work correctly and have security risks. However, it's not as easy as just to add '/' to delimiters, something like "<https://cert=>./path\_to\_cert;key=./path\_to\_key;@host:port/…" is commonly used to pass extra parameters to https protocol.

Try to workaround it this way:

- fix TParsedLocation for non-https protocols;

- for https, first try to parse url as earlier. If got userinfo starts with "cert=" or "key=", than we either have this specific variant of userinfo (and second '@' somewhere in the url won't break things), or have ill-formed url, that won't work with '@' or without;

- if userinfo doesn't match specific https pattern, then parse it again with '/' as delimiter. This fixes https without userinfo or with another userinfo.

author: orlovnikita <orlovnikita@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
hnsw - option to control return condition that is useful when there are deleted items

For hnsw without filtering the current condition is correct as there are only two cases:

1. `nearest.size() < searchNeighborhoodSize` =\> we push an object to `candidates` and to `nearest` and don't pop anything from `nearest` =\> set of `candidates` is included in `nearest` =\> the worst from `nearest` cannot be strictly better than the best from `candidates` =\> we continue our search

2. if we already have `searchNeighborhoodSize` this extra check does not make a difference

For the case with items marked as deleted an extra condition is necessary (this functionality is similar to filtering).

Suppose that we have one candidate E and two neighbors A and B, both candidates are marked deleted and further than E =\> nearest = \{E\}, candidates = \{A, B\}

Then `nearest.Top() = E` is closer than `candidates.top() = minDist{A, B}` =\> we return from the cycle immediately without the sufficient number of nearest objects.

author: orlovnikita <orlovnikita@yandex-team.com>
commit message:
hnsw - acorn filtering

We introduce filters support in HNSW runtime

User filters are represented by `IFilter` class

Filtering strategy is configured by `EFilterMode`

`EFilterMode::NO_FILTER` does not change current behavior and does not check filters in hnsw runtime

`EFilterMode::FILTER_NEAREST` - do not add nodes that do not pass filter to `nearest`, but add to candidates so that traversal continues to their neighbors until we reach at least `searchNeighborhoodSize`

`EFilterMode::ACORN` represents an implementation of ACORN 1 algorithm from article - <https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04871>

The core idea of the algorithm is to search two-hop neighbors when the first hop neighbor does not pass filter. When this strategy is used we do not add filtered docs to candidates

We also introduce an optimization to ACORN algorithm:

- If we've already seen a node as the first-hop neighbor we can just skip it

- Else if we've already checked filters for a node that passes filter we can skip it as its neighbors will still be traversed as we added this node to candidates

- Else if we are currently in the second-hop stage for a node that does not pass the filter and we already checked filters for it we can also skip

[util] the THashSet::operator== must compare elements using their comparison operators.

The C++ standard describes the requirements for comparing unordered containers in [unord.req.general]:
> Two unordered containers a and b compare equal if a.size() == b.size() and,
> for every equivalent-key group [Ea1, Ea2) obtained from a.equal_range(Ea1),
> there exists an equivalent-key group [Eb1, Eb2) obtained from b.equal_range(Ea1),
> such that is_permutation(Ea1, Ea2, Eb1, Eb2) returns true.

#else

After:

#if Y_HAS_CPP_ATTRIBUTE(attribute_name)
    // use
  #else
    // fallback

```

commit message:
Y_HAS_CPP_ATTRIBUTE macro

The new macro `Y_HAS_CPP_ATTRIBUTE` simplifies the check for C++ attribute support by handling nested `#if defined(__has_cpp_attribute)` checks.

Before:
```cpp
    #if defined(__has_cpp_attribute)
        #if __has_cpp_attribute(attribute_name)
           // use
        #else
           // fallback
        #endif
    #else
        // fallback
    #endif
```

After:
```cpp
    #if Y_HAS_CPP_ATTRIBUTE(attribute_name)
        // use
      #else
        // fallback
    #endif
```

The new macro also allows checking C++ attributes when compiling C code without raising errors related to different tokenization rules in these languages. Of course, such a test always returns `0` when compiling source code in C.

Also, rename `Y_HAVE_ATTRIBUTE` to `Y_HAS_ATTRIBUTE` for consistency.

author: Szabolcs Fazekas <szabolcs.fazekas@ahrefs.com>
commit message:
Fix Linux build failures caused by missing standard library linking

CatBoost v1.2.8 build was failing with undefined symbol linker errors on Linux
due to incomplete library linking configuration. The errors included:

- undefined symbol: fallocate64 (from glibc)
- undefined symbol: __isoc23_strtoll_l (from glibc locale functions)
- undefined symbol: pthread_getattr_np (from pthread extensions)
- undefined symbol: usleep (from POSIX standard library)
- undefined symbol: fchmod, sysinfo, flock (various system calls)

Root cause: The CMake configuration uses -nodefaultlibs to remove all default
library linking, but only re-adds pthread. This strips out essential system
libraries that contain the missing symbols.

Solution: Add essential system libraries back to the link configuration:
- libc (c): Standard C library containing most missing symbols
- libm (m): Math library for mathematical functions
- libdl (dl): Dynamic linker library for dlopen/dlsym
- librt (rt): POSIX realtime library for additional system functions

This change allows CatBoost v1.2.8 to build successfully on modern Linux
systems while maintaining the intended custom library linking behavior.

commit message:
Use openMINDS property names in almost all cases.

Previously, we used "name" instead of "full_name", "alias" instead of "short_name", and a couple of other substitutions
for backwards compatibility with pre-openMINDS schemas.

Since these variant names are very widely used, this commit also introduces aliases, so that the old names will still work.
The old names could be deprecated and phased out, or we could keep the aliases mechanism, as it might be useful in transitioning
between major versions of openMINDS.

commit message:
A better way to make openMINDS terminology instances available as fairgraph instances.

The previous approach of initialising the instances as each module was imported, implemented in [b25091a5] and [e4df6ff0], has the problem that it prematurely triggers the resolution of types (in Property definitions) from strings to classes, and so the properties retain the openMINDS classes rather than getting the fairgraph ones.

The new approach leaves initialisation of instances until after all modules have been imported and the registry correctly set up.

This also reverts [5853d18f], since those changes are not needed if all classes are properly initialised.

author: Tim Quelch <tim@tquelch.com>
commit message:
Ensure eigenvalues are positive in SPD matrices

By definition symmetric positive definite matrices have positive
eigenvalues. Numerical errors may result in infinitesimal negative
eigenvalues being computed, resulting in DomainErrors when the sqrt or
log of the eigenvalue is calculated.

This change replaces any negative eigenvalues with the smallest positive
value to ensure that the sqrt is successful.

This makes it the user's responsibility to ensure that input arguments
are valid SPDs before passing.

author: Ole Gunnar Røsholt Hovland <73483154+elorannug@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Removed expicit complex conjugate in Stiefel.jl documentation

Removed, because it should not be there. It now matches the description given in Generalized Stiefel. See below for a short proof. 

For some interval, $I=[a,b]$ where $a,b\in \mathbb{R}$, the parametrized curve is the smooth map $c\colon I\to \mathcal{M}$. It is $c(t)\in \operatorname{St}(n,k)$ where $c(0)=p$ and, the velocity of the curve is $c'(0)=X$. Since $c(t)$ is in $\operatorname{St}(n,k)$, it must satisfy
$c(t)^{\mathrm{H}}c(t)=I_{k}$ 
for all $t\in I$. Taking the derivative of with respect to $t$ at $t=0$ the expression becomes
$c'(t)^{\mathrm{H}}c(t)+c(t)^{\mathrm{H}}c'(t)=X^{\mathrm{H}}p+p^{\mathrm{H}}X=0_{k}.$
This means that the tangent space of $\operatorname{St}(n,k)$ at the point $p$ is
$\operatorname{T}_{p}\operatorname{St}(n,k)=\left\{ p \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times k}\;\middle|\;X^{\mathrm{H}}p=-p^{\mathrm{H}}X \right\}.$

author: zazabap <sweynan@icloud.com>
commit message:
Add CUDA extension for GPU-accelerated manifold operations

Add ManifoldsCUDAExt that provides GPU-compatible overrides for:
- QR retraction on GeneralUnitaryMatrices: avoids scalar indexing by
  extracting Q/R as dense CuArrays and using broadcasting for sign
  correction instead of Diagonal matrix multiply
- rand! for UnitaryMatrices: uses CUDA.randn for on-GPU random generation
  instead of CPU randn + transfer
- log_safe! for real matrices on GPU: routes through complex path since
  base implementation calls convert(Matrix, ...) forcing CPU

Primary targets are UnitaryMatrices(n), PowerManifold, and ProductManifold
as used by ParametricDFT.jl for quantum circuit optimization.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: zazabap <sweynan@icloud.com>
commit message:
Add CUDA extension tests

Test GPU operations on Euclidean, Sphere, and UnitaryMatrices(2):
- exp, retract (polar, QR), log, project, inner, norm
- Float32 and ComplexF64 element types
- PowerManifold with nested CuArrays
Tests are conditional on CUDA.functional().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: zazabap <sweynan@icloud.com>
commit message:
GPU-native exp!/log_safe! via eigendecomposition, add Grassmann tests

Replace CPU-fallback exp! with GPU-native Hermitian eigendecomposition
(for skew-Hermitian X: exp(X) = V*Diag(exp(-i*lambda))*V' via heevd!).
Replace CPU-fallback log_safe! with general eigendecomposition via geev!.
Add Grassmann QR retraction override for GPU. Trim docstrings.

47 tests: Euclidean (Float64/Float32, vector/matrix), Sphere,
UnitaryMatrices (exp, project, QR retraction, log), Grassmann
(exp, project, QR retraction), PowerManifold nested.
Zero CPU fallbacks — all computation stays on GPU.

commit message:
Changes for 0.2.3 release (#154)

- Adds the standard python `.gitignore` file
- Adds a `.github/` which holds template files for PRs  and guidelines for contributing to the code
- Adds Sphinx docs and ReadTheDocs to the repository
- Docstrings are now formatted in numpydoc style
- Code is styled in YAPF style; configured by the `setup.cfg` file
- Re-wrote the tests to use pytest
- Adds CodeCov to the repository
- Adds Versioneer to the repository
- Improvements to Travis-CI
   - Builds and deploys conda packages for py3.5/3.6 for both osx/linux platforms
   - Deploys the conda environment yml file onto anaconda cloud
   - Conda packages follow convention, example for version 0.2.3 on python3.5
      - `blues-0.2.3-py35g{SHORTHASH}_{#UNRELEASED COMMITS}` or `blues-0.2.3-py35g6aaba2d_5`
- Minor API changes, renaming some functions in the BLUESSimulation to adhere to conventional python name schemes
   - Move the `engine.py` module (which housed just one single class) into the `moves.py` module
   - Fix in the `AlchemicalExternalLangevinIntegrator` for issue #115 [ref](https://github.com/nathanmlim/blues/blob/8079e40bda8c092da65123722ba3b54376ea5268/blues/integrators.py#L136)
- Make package compatible for openmm=7.2.2 and openmmtools=0.15.0
- Includes changes from #150 
   - Removes some code redundancy in syncing the simulation states
   - Correctly resets the velocities before the start of each MD simulation [ref](https://github.com/MobleyLab/blues/blob/fix-0.2.3/blues/simulation.py#L1248)
   - Corrects behavior in syncing the simulation states [ref](https://github.com/MobleyLab/blues/blob/9172607d3b1d7941a894e51d130c85a77f1bbbac/blues/simulation.py#L1143)
   - Adds some checks in the freezing selection [ref](https://github.com/MobleyLab/blues/blob/9172607d3b1d7941a894e51d130c85a77f1bbbac/blues/simulation.py#L439)

author: Steven Ayoub <steven.ayoub.362@my.csun.edu>
commit message:
Initial implementation of Quaternion Rotation

Current implementation construct quaternion-based darts for MolDarting from a set of coordinate files.

Modified the move() to grab compute the relative pose of a ligand with respect to a protein-based local coordinate frame.

 The translation is done using the current ligand center of mass however the rotation still need some work

author: Steven Ayoub <ayoubsj@uci.edu>
commit message:
Apply quaternion-based ligand rotation using current protein anchor atoms

- Uses relative quaternion (q_target * q_current.inv()) to rotate ligand - Builds current protein local frame from anchor atoms (p1, p2, p3) - Translates rotated ligand to target COM using dart['translation'] projected through the protein frame

author: Jo Van Bulck <jo.vanbulck@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
Support for HW-level stack overflow protection.

Dedicated instruction (0x1388) sets internal "stack guard" register
to the value provided in r15. The CPU raises a violation for any SP
updates past the guard address.

NOTE: SMs are themselves responsible to correctly init the stack
guard address, but HW-level stack overflow detection is  a
necessary condition to prevent the secure IRQ logic from spilling
SM register contents into unprotected memory.

IRQs should only be served _after_ an SM has explicly enabled interrupts
(to indicate it has restored its internal call stack).

DINT only guarantees non-interruption one cycle _after_ completion, however.

author: Jo Van Bulck <jo.vanbulck@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
omsp_exec_unit: keep gie low one cycle after SM switch.

HW clears interrupts one cycle after entering an SM to allow software
to DINT before restoring SM-internal call stack and EINT.

Current solution is a bit hacky, but should be hidden by the compiler
to ensure attackers cannot abuse dint edge cases.

commit message:
Store the previous PC when a PM IRQ occurs

This way, the normal control flow access control logic can be used when
a RETI to PM is executed. Before, we used to store a single bit to
indicate that the previous instruction was a RETI to PM and the access
control logic would take that into account to allow jumps to non-entry
points.  However, this scheme is only secure with a single module. Also,
storing the previous PC more closely follows the model.

unit when interrupting a sancus_enable crypto instruction.

author: marton bognar <marton.bognar@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
Mitigation: Maximum instruction execution length

Introduced a Verilog parameter with the updated maximal instruction execution length, 7 cycles.
Keep in mind that this only fixes enclaves that write to program memory, but not enclaves
using cryptographic instructions.

author: marton bognar <marton.bognar@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
Mitigation: Resuming an enclave with reti multiple times

The hardware flag that indicates that an enclave has been interrupted is
now lowered during the corresponding reti, so later reti instructions
do not restore the shadow register file.

author: marton bognar <marton.bognar@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
Mitigation: Interrupts with the watchdog timer

The interrupt padding mechanism is now applied to interrupts scheduled by the watchdog timer.

author: marton bognar <marton.bognar@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
Mitigation: Enclave accessing unprotected memory

Enclave accesses to unprotected memory regions now cause a memory violation.

author: marton bognar <marton.bognar@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
Mitigation: Reentering enclave from ISR

Jumping to the entry point of the enclave while an enclave interrupt is being handled now results in a violation.
NOTE: This mitigation has only been tested on a system that supports a single enclave.

author: Jo Van Bulck <jo.vanbulck@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
Mitigation: constant instruction length following reti.

Non-jump instructions following reti first had to go through the E_JMP state
before getting into execution. E_JMP is now integrated into the final stage of
the reti instruction itself.

author: marton bognar <marton.bognar@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
Mitigation: Enclave mapping over the MMIO or IVT regions

Enclaves are now disallowed from (partially) mapping either their data or text sections over the memory-mapped I/O section or the interrupt vector table.

author: marton bognar <marton.bognar@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
Mitigation: Updating GIE from an enclave

Updates to the GIE bit in the status register are now ignored if the CPU is currently executing the enclave.

author: marton bognar <marton.bognar@cs.kuleuven.be>
commit message:
Mitigation: Multiple enclaves

The default number of supported enclaves is now restricted to 1.

author: guido <pe1nnz@amsat.org>
commit message:
Improved audio quality and IMD3 performance and experimental (amplitude) pre-distortion and calibration. Fixed an issue with spurious transmission for RX-TX-RX transitions.

In detail:
Reduced sample jitter by matching sampling rate to a multiple of OCR0A timer divider.
Unit angle now configurable and scalable so that full precision (of integer range) can be used to calculate phase differences; the unit angle is configured to be an exact multiple of the samp$
Hilbert transformer fixed bug, simplified and improved in precision (improved from -15dB to -40dB in an image rejection setting).
Arctan rounding errors reduced from approx. 5 degree to 0.8 degree.
Moved from 8 bit to 16 bit precision for audio input and I/Q values.
Microphone-input response now flat from 0-2200Hz (removed original high-pass filter with 20dB roll-off at 800Hz).
Experimental code (currently commented-out) for measuring phase differences between programmatically synchronised SI5351 clocks.
Fixed an issue where for every RX-TX transition a burst of random RF frequencies were emitted.
Improved precision of smeter, and found that disabling smeter prevent spurs leaking in from LCD data transfer into RXi (smeter still enabled).
Added a LUT-based pre-distortion algorithm that can be calibrated via an internal amplitude measurement.
Fixed issue with the envelope generation through Q6 impacting the IMD-performance, dynamic range, efficiency and thermal-stability; this fix REQUIRES the removal of C31 and increase of C32 to$
Fixed an issue where VOX was unintentially triggering TX by ADC noise leaking through key-shaping circuit, and simplied VOX algorithm.
Generaized PLL and MultiSynth algorithms and added experimental algorithm for setting a second frequency (via a different MS divider and where PLL is the same).
Experimental code for measuring the phase of the transmitted signal (via PA and QSD), this could give insight in antenna impedance and PA phase-response as function of amplitude.

commit message:
Add 1n capacitor between gates of PA and RX switch

Without this capacitor, using DC shorted antennas, such as magnetic loops, causes the RX BS170 to heat up and suck up RF, leading it to the demux chip and MCU.  Without the cap I also experienced problems where when/after TXing, the MCU would lock up or create glitchy noise that would be cleared by either reseting the radio, or by changing frequency.

commit message:
Build LUT by fixed point math

Step 1 to remove float from the code. LUT table can be perfect build by
fixed point math.

lut[i] = (float)i / ((float)255 / ((float)pwm_max - (float)pwm_min)) +
pwm_min;
can be converted to:
lut[i] = (float)i * ((float)pwm_max - (float)pwm_min) / (float)255 +
pwm_min;
can be futher convert to:
lut[i] = i * (pwm_max - pwm_min) / 255 + pwm_min;

The second convertion is validated by a small test code. The first
convertion has slight difference on lut[255] of some combinition of
pwm_max and pwm_min, which I believe second fomula is more accurate.

Continues ATT support

Combine the hardware and software ATT support into one single value to
be continues from 0 to -85db.

The hardware ATT is prefered and used first. The following tables
shows the caculation. The software ATT is changed to add two values
that are shift by certain bits. So that we can simulate 1-15 db ATT via
software.

shift0  shift1  ration  db
                1       0.00
1       2       0.75    -1.25
1       3       0.625   -2.04
        1       0.5     -3.01
2       3       0.375   -4.26
2       4       0.3125  -5.05
        2       0.25    -6.02
3       4       0.1875  -7.27
3       5       0.15625 -8.06
        3       0.125   -9.03
4       5       0.09375 -10.28
4       6       0.0781  -11.07
        4       0.0625  -12.04

0-12    => software
13 - 19 => -13 hardware + software
20 - 32 => -20 hardware + software
33 - 39 => -20 + -13 hardware + software
40 - 52 => -40 hardware + software
53 - 59 => -40 + -13 hardware + software
60 - 72 => -40 + -20 hardware + software
73 - 85 => -40 + -20 + -13 hardware + software -12

commit message:
multi-allelic compliance

This is the first step towards compliance with multi-allelic sites, as
is required by the VCF specification.  I am building on prior
modifications by Aaron Quinlan which enabled multiple alternates per
record.  Effectively, this change involves considering all fields in the
VCF, both INFO and individual sample fields, as vectors.

All included tools have been adjusted to use the new format.

Additionally, I am adding several scripts which assist in using the
previously included R scripts for genotype analysis.

update vcfstats to deal with "complex" events

These are alleles which can be interpreted as a block substitution or
multi-base change.  An example would be ATGG -> ACCAG.  The pairwise
alignment of these alleles suggests a mismatch and a gap.

Support is not perfect as pairwise alignment may generate complex
interpretations of some indels.  This should be enough to at least
collect basic statistics about the prevalence of these events in VCF
files.

commit message:
edge case fix, numbers as strings in vcffilter

If a number is provided for comparison with a string, the comparison will fail
because it first checks if both the variables being compared have the same
type.  We can deal with this by checking if one is a string and the other a
number at comparison time, and converting both into strings for comparison.
This allows user-expected behavior when doing things like:

    vcffilter -f "Q = 2"

When Q is a string variable in the VCF file.

commit message:
vcfglbound --- cap GLs and possibly exclude sites with GLs > 0

This normalization process is important when providing GLs as input to phasing
and imputation systems.

Normalization involves scaling all GLs by the max for the sample, so that the
max GL is represented as 0, maintaining the relative values of each GL.  Then,
GLs which are still below a given threshold are set to the threshold to prevent
underflow.  A suitable threshold for typical use is -10, but no defaults are
set in this application.

author: Alexander Regueiro <alexreg@gmail.com>
commit message:
Fix man page installation

The trailing slash in `${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/man/` is important, as we do not want to install the man pages in `${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/man/man1/man`, but rather just `${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/man/man1`. (I encountered this problem when building on macOS.)

Per the [documentation](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/command/install.html):

> The DIRECTORY form installs contents of one or more directories to a given destination. The directory structure is copied verbatim to the destination. The last component of each directory name is appended to the destination directory but a trailing slash may be used to avoid this because it leaves the last component empty.

author: Mathias Schmitt <mathiaspeterhorst@gmail.com>
commit message:
vcfflatten: fix segfault when no 'AF' field is present (#47).

vcfflatten crashed when 'flattening' a VCF file with more
than 2 alleles for a locus if no 'AF' field was present.
Add a new option to handle this behavior:
  - If the --ignore-errors option is passed to the program,
    do not try to flatten the offending line, and parse the
    next one.
  - if the --ignore-errors option is not passed, then the
    default behavior is to print an error message and
    exit.

commit message:
refactor(variant): Replace tabixpp with direct htslib in VariantCallFile interface

Replace tabixpp C++ wrapper with direct htslib integration:
- Replace Tabix* tabixFile with htslib members (htsFp, tbxIdx, tbxIter, tbxStr)
- Update includes from <tabix.hpp> to htslib headers
- Initialize new members in constructor with NULL/zero values
- Add proper htslib cleanup in destructor
- Move openTabix() from inline to declaration-only

This change prepares for CSI index support and removes a dependency layer.

author: ASLeonard <alexander.leonard@usys.ethz.ch>
commit message:
refactor(variant): Implement htslib-based indexed file operations

Implement direct htslib integration for indexed VCF access:
- openTabix(): Use hts_open() and tbx_index_load() with exception-based error handling
- parseHeader()/getHeaderLinesFromFile(): Read headers using hts_getline() and store first non-header line
- getNextVariant(): Use tbx_itr_next() for region queries and hts_getline() for sequential reading
- setRegion(): Use tbx_itr_querys() with proper iterator lifecycle management
- file_pos(): Use bgzf_tell() directly

Removes dependency on tabixpp wrapper while maintaining all functionality.

author: ASLeonard <alexander.leonard@usys.ethz.ch>
commit message:
build(cmake): Remove tabixpp dependency and modernize htslib linking

Remove tabixpp from build system and modernize dependency management:
- Replace pkg_check_modules(tabixpp) with pkg_check_modules(libdeflate)
- Remove tabixpp local build detection and source inclusion logic
- Consolidate htslib linking to directly link dependencies into vcflib
- Add conditional libdeflate support for local htslib builds
- Simplify vcflib_LIBS to only CMAKE_THREAD_LIBS_INIT
- Add Python finding configuration and gate pybind11 tests behind pybind11_FOUND

Enables CSI index support and simplifies the dependency chain.
